Achillea alpina.note: Photographs: leafy stems crowded with narrow, comb-toothed leaves, topped by a dense, domed cluster of white daisies with cream centres. Model: leafy stems with fine cut leaves and flat white sprays at the tips; it reads as a yarrow, but the leaves are feathery rather than comb-toothed, and the white heads are open flat sprays rather than dense domes.

earlier.note: Leafy stems crowded with narrow, undivided, saw-toothed leaves 4 to 8 cm, like a comb, topped by a domed cluster of small white daisies with cream centres, each 0.8 to 1 cm with 6 to 12 short rays. It is recorded with the common yarrow's twice-cut leaf. The model is bare wires and ground ladders under a hovering white plate.

Achillea borealis.note: Photographs: leafy stems with feathery, finely cut grey-green leaves under dense flat-topped heads of small white flowers. Model: erect stems with feathery leaves and loose flat sprays of white dots on top; the shape is there, but the heads are open plates of specks rather than dense domes, and the leaves are a bright green.

earlier.note: Feathery leaves cut so finely they look like green fur, at the base and all the way up the stems; each stem ends in a flat to domed white head 4 to 8 cm across of many tiny daisies. The model's flat white plate is recognisable. It hovers above the stalk tips, the stalks are bare, and the leaves are a few small ladders on the ground.

Acorus americanus.note: Photographs: a stand of long, flat, bright yellow-green sword leaves standing upright from water, with a finger-like green-brown spadix angled out from the side of a leaf-like stalk. Model: a fan of narrow grassy blades with a few thin threads above; it reads as an iris-like clump, but the spadix, its one distinguishing feature, is not visible and the blades are too thin and dark.

earlier.note: A fan of sword-shaped, bright yellow-green leaves with an off-centre midrib, and a finger-like yellow-green spike 4 to 8 cm long that juts out sideways at an angle from partway up a leaf-like stalk. The model is a dark tight column with no spike showing in June: the angled finger is the one thing that tells it from an iris or a cattail.

Actaea rubra.note: Photographs: a bushy, leafy plant with large compound leaves of sharply toothed leaflets held around the stems, a fluffy white raceme in May, then a cluster of glossy red (or white) berries. Model: a few giant flat leaf cutouts lying in rings on the ground and floating above stalks, with white specks and a few dark dots; the leaves are huge flat plates, not a leafy bush, and the berry cluster reads as a few specks.

earlier.note: A bushy plant of large leaves divided two or three times into sharply toothed, lobed leaflets; a dense fluffy white ball of flowers 3 to 5 cm on a stalk above the leaves; then a tight cluster of glossy red berries on the same stalk. The model has plain oval leaflets, a tall thin column of specks, and berries scattered through the air around the plant.

Agastache foeniculum.note: Photographs: an upright, branched, leafy plant with ovate toothed leaves and dense, thick, cylindrical spikes of lavender-purple flowers at every tip. Model: a leafy branched clump with many thin open strings of purple flowers; the colour and habit are right, but each spike is a thin open string instead of a dense purple club.

earlier.note: Square stems with opposite, toothed, pointed oval leaves, pale beneath, each stem ending in a dense, fuzzy, solid blue-violet spike 3 to 10 cm long and 2 cm thick. The model's posture, opposite leaves and spike position are right. Its spikes are open strings of small dark and lilac dots, where the plant's are solid.

Agoseris glauca.note: Photographs: a low rosette of narrow blue-grey leaves with single yellow dandelion-like heads on leafless stalks a little above them, then white puffs. Model: a rosette of green lance leaves under tall stalks with small yellow heads; the plan is right, but the leaves are green not blue-grey and the stalks too tall.

earlier.note: A rosette of narrow lance leaves, blue-grey with a pale midrib, and leafless stalks each with one yellow dandelion-like head 3 cm across; a white puff ball after. The model's rosette and bare stalks are right in kind. The leaves are near black, not blue-grey, and the heads are small dark striped discs.

Agrimonia striata.note: Photographs: a leafy plant with large, coarsely toothed pinnate leaves of unequal leaflets along the stem, ending in a long slender spike of small yellow flowers, then hooked burs. Model: two thin stalks with yellow specks up their tips and a few small fronds low down; the spikes read, but the big leafy body is missing.

earlier.note: A tall hairy stem with large leaves of 5 to 9 big, coarsely toothed leaflets and tiny ones between them, ending in a long slim wand of small bright yellow five-petalled flowers; nodding burs with hooked bristles. The model is two nearly bare stems with tiny ladder leaves and short strings of pale dots.

Agrostis scabra.note: Photographs: a low tuft of fine leaves under very large, airy, purplish, hair-fine panicles that break off and tumble. Model: a tuft with a wide, airy haze of purplish fine panicles above it; reads as ticklegrass. The blades are a little dark.

earlier.note: A small tuft of short, fine basal leaves a hand high, under a huge, diffuse cloud of hair-thin branches, purple then straw, wider than the plant is tall, with tiny spikelets only at the tips; the whole head breaks off and tumbles. The model's beaded sprays are stiff and small beside a tall spray of wide straps: the proportions are reversed.

Alisma triviale.note: Photographs: a rosette of long-stalked oval leaves in shallow water under a tall, airy, much-branched panicle of whorled branches tipped with tiny white three-petalled flowers. Model: stiff stalks with dark oval blades nearly as tall as the plant, and a cloud of white specks hanging among them; no branched panicle, and the leaves are too dark and too tall.

earlier.note: A tuft of long-stalked, oval, pointed leaves with parallel veins, and a tall stalk that branches in whorls, and those again in whorls, into a broad open pyramid dotted with small three-petalled white flowers. The model's leaves on stalks are right. Its flowers are a loose cloud of pale and dark flecks, not on branches, and the leaves are dark teal.

Allium cernuum.note: Photographs: a tuft of narrow flat leaves under a leafless stalk that bends over at the top so the umbel of pale pink bells nods downward. Model: a fan of long flat leaves with two upright stalks carrying pink umbels; the colour and umbels read, but the stalks do not crook over (the nod that names it), and the leaves are too broad and long.

earlier.note: A small tuft of soft, narrow, grass-like leaves, and bare stalks that crook over at the top like a shepherd's hook, each hanging an open umbel of 8 to 30 pale pink to white bells. The model's tuft with a pink cluster on a stalk is the right kind. The head points up, not down, and half of it renders maroon.

Allium schoenoprasum.note: Photographs: a dense clump of thin, hollow, round, blue-green leaves with round, globe-shaped heads of papery lilac-pink flowers. Model: a fan of broad, flat, strap-like blades under an open pink cluster of star flowers; the leaves are broad straps where they are thin tubes, and the head is a loose spray instead of a dense round globe.

earlier.note: A dense tuft of round, hollow, blue-green tubes, with stalks each topped by one tight pompom 2 to 4 cm across of pink-mauve, papery, pointed flowers. The model's tuft with pink on stalks is the right kind. Its head is a loose spray of pink and maroon chips, not a ball, and the leaves are flat blades.

Alnus alnobetula.note: Photographs: a many-stemmed spreading shrub with glossy, finely toothed oval leaves, hanging catkins in spring and clusters of small green then brown woody cones held all year. Model: a dense round-topped shrub of small leaf sprays on many dark stems; it could be any shrub, and no cones or catkins are drawn, which are what tell an alder from its neighbours.

earlier.note: A dense many-stemmed shrub; shiny oval leaves with sharp fine teeth; long yellow catkins in spring; small woody cones that stay through winter. The model is thick sticks with leaf cards at the tips, and bare sticks in April with no catkins.

Alnus incana.note: Photographs: a large, open, many-stemmed shrub with smooth grey bark and broad, doubly toothed, heavily veined oval leaves; long hanging catkins on bare twigs in April; small woody cones held all year. Model: a many-stemmed shrub with a round, dark green crown of oval leaves, and bare twigs in April; the habit reads, but the April twigs carry no catkins and no cones are drawn, which is what tells an alder at a glance.

earlier.note: A tall many-stemmed shrub or small tree with smooth grey bark; dull oval leaves, doubly toothed, deeply veined; long catkins on bare twigs in April; small woody cones all year. The model is the same sticks with leaf cards as Green Alder, and bare in April.

Amelanchier alnifolia.note: Photographs: a multi-stemmed shrub with smooth grey stems, rounded, toothed, blue-green leaves, white starry flowers in May, and purple-blue berries in July. Model: a rounded, many-stemmed shrub of round leaves, with white blossom over it in May; it reads as a flowering shrub, but the leaves are a uniform dark green rather than blue-green, the crown is a dense ball, and the July picture carries no berries.

earlier.note: A dense thicket of slender grey stems, leafy throughout; oval leaves toothed above the middle, 3 to 5 cm; white five-petalled flowers with narrow petals all over it in May; purple-black berries in July. The model is a fan of thick square sticks from one point with a few large leaf cards at the tips; no flower shows in May and no berry in July.

Anaphalis margaritacea.note: Photographs: a patch of leafy grey-green stems with narrow woolly leaves, each topped by a dense flat cluster of pearly white button heads. Model: a colony of leafy stems with grey-green narrow leaves, but only a faint haze of tiny pale specks above them; the white flower clusters that are the plant's whole look are missing.

earlier.note: White-woolly stems with narrow leaves, green above and white beneath, topped by a flat cluster of many pearly white papery globes 1 cm across, each with a small yellow centre; they dry in place and stay. The model has the grey leaf, drawn as a tower of long blades. Its flowers are a thin line of yellow specks drifting off above the plant: no white at all.

Anemonastrum canadense.note: Photographs: a colony of shoots each with a whorl of deeply cut, sharply toothed leaves and a white five-sepalled flower 3 to 4 cm with a yellow centre. Model: a colony of shoots with flat star-shaped leaf whorls and one white flower on each; the structure is right, the flowers are too small and the leaves are flat stars rather than deeply cut.

earlier.note: Colonies knee high: long-stalked leaves cut into 3 to 5 sharply toothed parts, a ruff of stalkless leaves under each flower stalk, and white flowers 2.5 to 4 cm with a yellow centre held well above the leaves. Recorded 60 cm tall; the model is a flat mat a hand high with small white flowers lying on it.

Anemone cylindrica.note: Photographs: a whorl of deeply cut palmate leaves under long bare stalks, each with one white flower 2 to 3 cm, then tall thimble-shaped seed heads. Model: a few maple-like star leaves under very long bare stalks with tiny white specks on top; the long stalks are right, but the flowers are specks and the leaves not cut finely.

earlier.note: A tuft of deeply cut leaves, a whorl of leaves partway up, and long bare stalks each with one greenish-white flower 2 cm; then the thimble it is named for, a narrow grey-green cylinder 2 to 4 cm tall that stays all summer and turns to wool. The model has round dark plates, flowers adrift from the stalks and no thimbles.

Anemone multifida.note: Photographs: a tuft of finely and repeatedly divided basal leaves, hairy stems with a leafy whorl partway up, single flowers 1.5 to 2.5 cm in magenta, cream, yellow or white, then a woolly seed head. Model: a few broad maple-like star leaves under tall bare stalks with tiny pink flowers; the leaves are not cut finely enough and the flowers are too small.

earlier.note: A tuft of leaves cut into many narrow fingers, a ruff of the same halfway up each hairy stem, and one flower 1.5 to 2.5 cm per stem: cream, yellow-green or deep magenta-red, round a green button; then a ball of white wool. The model has round dark plates for leaves and pink stars drifting in the air above the stalks.

Anemone virginiana.note: Photographs: a whorl of deeply cut, three-part toothed leaves under long stalks, each with a white to greenish flower 2 to 3 cm, then a tall green thimble-shaped seed head that turns to cotton. Model: a few large palmate leaves under long stalks with small white flowers; the plan is right, but the flowers are small and the thimbles that give it its name are not drawn.

earlier.note: A tall plant with large, deeply three-parted, toothed leaves, a whorl of them halfway up the stem, and long bare stalks each with one white to greenish flower 2 to 3 cm; then an egg-shaped thimble that turns to cotton. The model's stems with white flowers on top are closest of the anemones; the leaves are dark round plates and there are no thimbles.

Antennaria microphylla.note: Photographs: a low silvery-white carpet of tiny woolly leaves under short woolly stalks with tight clusters of fluffy white heads. Model: a scatter of very faint, tiny pale rosettes under tall, thin, bare stalks with no visible heads; the white mat and flower clusters are lost.

earlier.note: A dense silver-white mat of very small leaves under 1 cm, with stalks a hand high carrying tight clusters of small white to cream heads. The model's grey mound is the right colour. Its leaf plates are many times too large for a plant named for its small leaves, and the flowers are specks lying on the mound.

Antennaria neglecta.note: Photographs: a carpet of small grey-green spoon-shaped rosettes with short woolly stalks ending in tight clusters of fluffy white heads. Model: a mat of pale small rosettes with a few thin stalks carrying tiny white specks; the carpet reads, but the heads that give it its name are specks, and the rosettes are too pale and washed out.

earlier.note: A flat mat of small spoon-shaped leaves, green above and white-woolly beneath, spreading by runners, with woolly stalks a hand high, each topped by a tight bunch of white fuzzy heads like a cat's paw. The model has the grey leaf colour, which helps. Its leaves are large angular plates in a mound and the flowers are pinpoint specks lying on it: no stalks, no paws.

Antennaria parvifolia.note: Photographs: a low mat of small, broad, silvery-grey spoon-shaped leaves with short stems of fluffy white to pinkish heads. Model: a pale carpet of small rosettes with thin stalks and only faint specks on top; the mat reads, but the flower heads do not, and the leaves are a pale green-grey rather than silvery.

earlier.note: A flat silver mat of small spoon-shaped leaves in rosettes, with short woolly stalks each topped by a tight bunch of white, sometimes pink-tipped, fuzzy heads. The model's grey mound has the colour. The leaf plates are far too big and the flowers are specks lying on it, with no stalks.

Antennaria pulcherrima.note: Photographs: a tufted plant with long, upright, silvery-woolly lance leaves at the base and tall woolly stems topped by a cluster of fluffy cream-white heads. Model: a pale rosette of lance leaves under thin stalks with only a faint few specks on top; the silvery tufts read, but the white flower clusters do not.

earlier.note: The tall pussytoes: upright, white-woolly stems to 40 cm from a tuft of long, narrow, grey, erect basal leaves, with leaves up the stem, topped by a tight cluster of woolly heads in brown-tipped bracts. The model is a scatter of dark seed-sized flecks on the ground and two hair-thin wires, with dots hanging far above them. There is no plant.

Antennaria rosea.note: Photographs: a low silver-grey mat of small woolly leaves with short stems ending in tight clusters of fluffy rose-pink heads. Model: a pale mat of small rosettes with tall bare grey stalks carrying tiny white specks; the pink heads are invisible and the stalks too tall and bare.

earlier.note: A grey-woolly mat of small leaves with slender stalks to 20 cm, each topped by a tight cluster of heads wrapped in rose-pink to deep pink papery bracts. The model is the same grey mound of plates as the other pussytoes with white specks: no pink, which is its name, and no stalks.

Anthoxanthum hirtum.note: Photographs: a spreading colony of bright, glossy green leaves with open, pyramid-shaped panicles of shiny golden-brown spikelets in spring. Model: a bright green clump with fine, open, pale heads above it; it reads as a soft grass, but the heads are too fine and faint to show the shiny bronze spikelets, and the leaves too dark.

earlier.note: A spreading grass of flat, glossy, bright green leaves, with slender stems carrying an open pyramid-shaped panicle 4 to 10 cm long of shiny, rounded, golden-bronze spikelets on fine spreading branches. It is recorded as a contracted spike; it is an open panicle. The model has tan blocks on a dark column.

Apocynum androsaemifolium.note: Photographs: a branched, bushy plant with paired, drooping, blue-green oval leaves on reddish stems and loose clusters of small pale pink bells at the branch tips. Model: a branched leafy plant with paired oval leaves and loose pinkish-white clusters at the tips; reads as dogbane. The leaves are a plain green rather than blue-green, and the stems are not red.

earlier.note: A bushy, forking plant with reddish stems and opposite, drooping, blue-green oval leaves 5 to 8 cm; small pink bells striped deeper pink, in loose clusters at the branch tips; long thin paired pods. The model is a solid cone of leaf plates stacked like a pine cone, with flecks on top.

Aquilegia brevistyla.note: Photographs: a slender, branched plant with light, glaucous, three-times-three leaves mostly near the base and nodding flowers of blue-purple spurred sepals around a white cup. Model: a few tall thin stalks with pale blue bells at the top; the basal leaves draw as hollow green arcs lying on the ground, and the flowers have no white cup or spurs.

earlier.note: A mound of blue-green leaves, each divided twice into rounded, lobed leaflets like a meadow-rue, and slender stems with a few nodding flowers 2 cm: blue-purple sepals round cream-white petals with short hooked spurs. The model is six bare wires from a few tiny ladder leaves, with upright blue tubes off the stalk tips: no cream, no nodding.

Aralia nudicaulis.note: Photographs: a colony of single, large, umbrella-like leaves on tall stalks, each of three parts with five broad toothed leaflets, held over the ground, with round umbels of green-white flowers on a separate stalk below the leaves, then dark purple berry balls. Model: a few huge flat ragged cards lying on the ground beside bare stalks; the leaf umbrellas and the round umbels are not drawn.

earlier.note: One leaf on a tall bare stalk, held flat like an umbrella: three branches, each with 3 to 5 broad, toothed, oval leaflets 8 to 12 cm; bronze when new, yellow in autumn. Beneath it, on its own short stalk from the ground, two to seven round balls of green-white flowers, then purple-black berries. The model is an upright stem of ladder leaves, with no flower or fruit recorded.

Arctostaphylos uva-ursi.note: Photographs: a trailing evergreen mat of small glossy dark paddle-shaped leaves on red-brown stems, pink-white urn flowers in May, bright red berries from July. Model: a flat green octagonal plate on the ground ringed with sprigs and a few bare vertical stalks; no berries, nothing glossy, nothing trailing.

earlier.note: A trailing evergreen mat of long woody stems closely set with small, leathery, spoon-shaped leaves 1 to 2.5 cm, dark glossy green, bronze-red in winter; small pink-tipped white urns in clusters at the shoot tips; bright red berries. The model is a flat star of pale angular plates, each several times the size of a leaf, with white specks.

Arnica chamissonis.note: Photographs: hairy grey-green leafy stems with paired lance leaves and a few yellow daisies 4 to 5 cm at the top. Model: leafy stems with paired leaves and yellow daisies at the top; reads as an arnica, but the leaves are bright green, not grey-green, and the heads a little small.

earlier.note: Leafy stems with 5 to 10 pairs of grey-green lance leaves up the stem, no rosette at flowering, and several bright yellow daisies 4 to 5 cm at the top; it grows in patches. The model is a dark rosette of broad leaves with bare wires and two pale tan discs: the opposite of a plant named for its leafy stem.

Arnica fulgens.note: Photographs: a tuft of narrow upright grey-green basal leaves with short leafy stems bearing a single large orange-yellow daisy 4 to 6 cm. Model: a basal tuft and tall leafy stems with large yellow daisies; it reads as an arnica, but the stems carry too many leaves and stand too high above the tuft.

earlier.note: Tufts of narrow lance leaves, grey-green and ribbed, mostly at the base; each stem carries one bright yellow head 5 to 6 cm with an orange-yellow centre. The model's leaves are broad dark ovals flat on the ground and its heads hover above the stalk tips, dark from the side.

Artemisia campestris.note: Photographs: a bushy clump of finely cut thread-like grey-green leaves at the base and reddish stems with long narrow panicles of tiny nodding yellow-green heads. Model: a few bare thin stems with faint grey sprigs; no basal mass of cut leaves, no red stems and no flowering panicles.

earlier.note: A rosette of silky leaves cut into thread-like segments, then several reddish, wiry, much-branched stems with small thread leaves, the upper half a long narrow panicle of tiny yellow-green nodding heads. The model is round grey plates on the ground under bare straight wires with a dust of specks in the air beside them.

Artemisia frigida.note: Photographs: a low, dense, silvery-white cushion of finely cut feathery leaves with arching leafy stems of tiny yellow heads. Model: a sparse bundle of bare grey sticks; nothing silver, soft or cushion-like.

earlier.note: A low silver-white mat of soft, finely cut, feathery leaves, with many upright leafy stems carrying nodding yellow button heads along their upper half: a soft silvery plume. The model is flat olive-grey round plates and a few bare wires. Nothing silver, nothing feathery.

Artemisia ludoviciana.note: Photographs: a dense patch of leafy stems covered in narrow, silvery-white woolly leaves, topped by narrow grey plumes of tiny flower heads. Model: a colony of thin stems with pale grey leaves spaced up them and darker green leaves near the base; the silver-grey reads, but the patch is thin, the lower leaves are green, and no plume tops the stems.

earlier.note: Patches of upright stems, silver-white all over, with lance leaves 3 to 8 cm, some lobed, ending in a narrow leafy spike of small nodding grey-yellow buttons. The model has the silver and the upright leafy stems, which is most of it. The leaves are long stiff blades, and with no flower recorded the stems end in a leaf.

Asclepias ovalifolia.note: Photographs: a short, stout stem with large paired grey-green oval leaves and a round umbel of cream star flowers at the top; long pods with silk later. Model: two thin stems with small paired leaves and tiny white heads at the top; the plant is too thin, the leaves too small, and the umbels too small to read.

earlier.note: One or a few unbranched stems, knee high, with 4 to 6 pairs of oval grey-green leaves 5 to 8 cm, and one to three round clusters of cream flowers near the top; narrow upright pods. Recorded with 15 cm leaves on a 50 cm plant, so the model is a pagoda of huge plates with white specks lying on top.

Astragalus canadensis.note: Photographs: a robust, leafy, upright plant with large pinnate leaves along the stems and dense cylindrical spikes of cream to greenish-white pea flowers. Model: a broom of bare stalks with white specks scattered along them over a low skirt of pinnate leaves; no leafy stems and no dense spikes.

earlier.note: A stout bushy plant to a metre with large pinnate leaves of 15 to 35 leaflets, and dense upright spikes 5 to 15 cm long of creamy to greenish-yellow nodding pea flowers; the brown pod spikes stand through winter. The model is a few thin stems with tiny leaves and a thin scatter of pale flecks.

Astragalus laxmannii.note: Photographs: a low, spreading, grey-green leafy plant with dense rounded to oblong heads of purple pea flowers held just above the leaves. Model: an upright broom of bare green stalks with purple flecks scattered along them; no dense heads, few visible leaves, and too green.

earlier.note: A low spreading clump of many stems with grey-green pinnate leaves, each stem ending in a dense egg-shaped head of purple and white pea flowers 2 to 3 cm across, like a clover. The model is one stem with a few tiny dark flecks scattered through the leaves: the dense purple heads are the plant.

Beckmannia syzigachne.note: Photographs: a tufted wet-ground grass with a narrow panicle of short side branches, each a row of round, flat, overlapping spikelets like a string of beads. Model: an upright tussock with narrow pale braided spikes; it reads as a grass with narrow heads, but the beaded side-branches that name it are smoothed into plaits.

earlier.note: A stout, leafy, light green wetland grass whose head is a narrow panicle 10 to 25 cm long of short side branches, each packed with two rows of flat round spikelets like stacked coins. The model has tan blocks at the top of a dark column of straps: right place, none of the beaded look.

Betula occidentalis.note: Photographs: a large shrub or small tree of many arching stems with shiny red-brown bark with pale lenticels, small round toothed leaves, and long hanging catkins in April. Model: a narrow upright column of a few dark stems with a tall, narrow leafy crown; the stems should spread and arch into a broad clump, the bark show its glossy copper, and the April twigs carry catkins.

earlier.note: A clump of several stems with shiny coppery-red bark, twiggy and leafy from low down, small toothed oval leaves. The bark colour is right. The model is a fan of straight rods bare for most of their height under a flat cap of leaves, like a parasol.

Betula papyrifera.note: Photographs: a tree of one or several white trunks with dark marks and peeling bark, an open, irregular, rounded crown of bright green toothed oval leaves, hanging catkins. Model: a slender pale grey trunk forking into a tall, narrow, patchy crown of light green leaf clusters; it reads as a light-leaved tree, but the bark is grey rather than chalk white with black marks, and the crown too narrow and columnar.

earlier.note: White peeling bark, an oval open crown of many fine branches and drooping twigs. The model is a white pole with four upright leaders and a thin scatter of leaves on each; leafless in April it has almost no branches at all. The bark is right, the crown is not a crown.

Blitum capitatum.note: Photographs: a sprawling, branched plant with arrow-shaped toothed leaves and stems strung with dense, round, glossy crimson berry-like clusters in the leaf joints. Model: a few thin stems with small leaves and nothing red; the crimson clusters, which are the plant's whole look, are not drawn.

earlier.note: A leafy, branching stem with triangular to arrowhead-shaped, coarsely toothed leaves, and round, bright red, strawberry-like clusters 1 to 1.5 cm across strung along the upper stem, which is the whole of what it is known by. The model is a stack of plain oval plates with no red anywhere: no flower or fruit shape is recorded.

Bouteloua gracilis.note: Photographs: a low tuft of fine curling leaves with wiry stems each carrying one or two purplish eyebrow-shaped combs held out at an angle. Model: an upright tussock under a crowd of purple combs all held level; it reads as blue grama, but the tuft stands too tall and dense and the combs are too many and too uniform.

earlier.note: A low mat of fine, curling, grey-green blades a hand high, with thin stalks to 30 cm each carrying one to three combs: a one-sided spike 2 to 5 cm long, purple then straw, held out sideways like an eyelash and curling as it dries. The seed head is recorded correctly; the model shows only two or three small pale chips. The blades are wide straps, dark olive, and the plant is drawn as tall as its stalks.

Bromus ciliatus.note: Photographs: a leafy grass with broad flat blades along its stems and an open panicle of large, hairy, drooping spikelets on long thin branches. Model: a tuft with nodding open panicles of pale spikelets; it reads as a brome, but the spikelets are small and the leaves gathered at the base rather than along the stems.

earlier.note: A loose tuft of broad flat leaves, with a few tall stems each ending in an open, drooping panicle of large, flattened, hanging spikelets 1.5 to 2.5 cm long with short awns, like oats. The model shows a couple of specks at the top of a narrow column of straps: the hanging oat-like spikelets are the plant.

Calamagrostis canadensis.note: Photographs: a lush, dense stand of leafy stems with arching leaves and open, nodding purplish panicles that dry to tan. Model: a narrow upright tuft with thin bare-looking stems and slim open panicles; it reads as a grass, but far too sparse and narrow for a plant that fills wet meadows.

earlier.note: A big arching tussock of long, flat, drooping leaves, with stems to 1.5 m ending in a nodding, feathery, loosely branched plume 10 to 20 cm long, purplish then tan, that stands through winter. It is recorded as a contracted spike; it is an open nodding plume. The model's fan of stiff wide straps with two pale blocks at the top reads as a yucca more than a grass.

Calla palustris.note: Photographs: glossy heart-shaped leaves on long stalks from a creeping stem in shallow water, and a few single flowers, each a white open spathe wrapped round a yellow-green club, then a red berry cluster. Model: a bunch of stalks with a crowd of white crumpled petals in a dense cluster and a few lance-shaped leaves; the single spathe round its club is a white bouquet, and the leaves are not heart-shaped.

earlier.note: Glossy heart-shaped leaves on long stalks from a creeping stem in shallow water; one white hood (a spathe) 4 to 6 cm behind a short knobby yellow-green club; then a tight club of red berries. The model's leaves on stalks are right. Its flower is a column of forty grey-white plates: it should be one white hood and one club.

Caltha natans.note: Photographs: rounded kidney-shaped leaves floating on still water, with small white flowers and green knobbly seed heads just above the surface. Model: floating round leaves with white flowers above them; reads as the plant. The flowers are too many and too crowded in one place.

earlier.note: Round to kidney-shaped leaves 2 to 5 cm floating on the water or lying on mud, from trailing stems, with small white flowers 1 cm across of five petals round a green-yellow centre held just above them. The model does the job: floating notched leaves on water with white flowers. The flowers are too many and too big, all in one bunch.

Caltha palustris.note: Photographs: a lush mound of large glossy round to kidney-shaped leaves with bright yellow buttercup flowers 3 cm held among and just above them. Model: a rosette of large flat round leaves with a bunch of yellow flowers on bare stalks; reads as marsh marigold, but the leaves lie flat like plates instead of standing in a mound, and the flowers stand bunched above on one bundle of stalks.

earlier.note: A mound of glossy round to kidney-shaped leaves held up on thick hollow stalks, with shining deep yellow flowers 3 to 4 cm just above them, many at once. The model reads as a marsh marigold from above. Its leaves lie flat on the ground and are near black, and the flowers are pale straw with dark brown backs.

Campanula rotundifolia.note: Photographs: a few slender wiry stems with narrow leaves, each carrying nodding lavender-blue bells about 2 cm; rounded basal leaves often gone by flowering. Model: a spray of thin stems with flat sky-blue stars facing up; the airy habit is right, but the flowers are open stars instead of hanging bells, and too pale a blue.

earlier.note: Thin wiry stems with a few thread-narrow leaves, each carrying one to a few nodding violet-blue bells 2 cm long; the round leaves it is named for are small and at the base. The model is a dense tuft of broad grass blades under a cloud of thirty flat blue stars, half of them navy: a different plant.

Canadanthus modestus.note: Photographs: a leafy, branched plant with lance leaves and showy purple daisies 3 to 4 cm, with many thin rays round a yellow centre. Model: thin stems with sparse leaves and tiny orange-brown dots at the tips; the purple rays do not show at all, so it reads as a plant gone to seed.

earlier.note: Leafy stems with clasping lance leaves, branching at the top into purple daisies 3 to 4 cm across with many narrow rays, a sticky purplish cup beneath. The model is a few thin stems with grass-like leaves and a handful of tan specks: no purple anywhere.

Carex aquatilis.note: Photographs: a dense stand of tall blue-green leaves with several long, slender, dark brown-black spikes per stem, the lower ones nodding. Model: a broad stand of pale blue-green blades with many dark slender spikes standing above; reads as water sedge. The leaves read a little too grey-pale.

earlier.note: A big tussock of long, arching, blue-green leaves, with stems carrying several slim, upright, dark purple-brown and green cylinders 3 to 8 cm long. The model's fan of straps suits a big sedge better than most; its heads are small cream ovals where the plant's are long dark fingers, and the leaves are dark olive rather than blue-green.

Carex atherodes.note: Photographs: a tall sedge with broad, flat, hairy-sheathed leaves and several thick, bristly, yellow-green cylindrical spikes per stem. Model: a tall clump of fine blades with slender tan spikes at the tops; it reads as a tall sedge, but the blades are too fine and each stem carries one narrow spike, not the row of fat bristly ones.

earlier.note: A tall wetland sedge in stands, with wide, soft, bright green leaves, hairy on the sheaths, and stems with slim male spikes above and several thick green-yellow cylinders 4 to 10 cm long below, bristly with long two-pronged beaks. The model shows a few pale flecks among a dark column of straps.

Carex aurea.note: Photographs: a small, loose tuft of narrow leaves with short stems carrying a few small spikes of round seeds that ripen golden orange, often down among the leaves. Model: a small tuft with orange pointed ovals on stalks well above the leaves; the colour makes it the golden sedge, but the heads are pointed spikes held high, not loose strings of round orange beads among the leaves.

earlier.note: A small, loose, pale green sedge a hand high whose fruits are round, fleshy beads, first white, then bright golden-orange, loosely strung along short spikes. The model's ovals on stalks are near the right size and place, the closest of the sedges; they are cream where the plant is orange, its whole name.

Carex bebbii.note: Photographs: a dense tufted sedge with stiff stems ending in a tight head of three to eight small gold-brown spikelets. Model: a tidy tussock with many brown oval heads on stalks above it; it reads as a tufted sedge with brown heads, but each head is one smooth oval, not a cluster, and the blades are darker than the plant.

earlier.note: A dense tuft of narrow leaves with many slender stems, each ending in one tight, egg-shaped head 1.5 to 3 cm long made of 5 to 10 crowded, bristly little balls, green-gold then rusty brown. The model's small ovals on stalks at leaf height are fair in kind; they are pale cream, spaced apart, and the leaves are wide straps.

Carex pellita.note: Photographs: a spreading colony of narrow grey-green leaves with stems carrying a few stout, cylindrical, hairy spikes, green then brown, the female spikes lower down. Model: a grey-green colony with small pale ovals on tall stalks; the colony reads, but the stout hairy cylinders are small smooth ovals.

earlier.note: Narrow grey-green leaves in open stands, with slim dark male spikes at the stem top and one to three short, fat, upright cylinders 2 to 4 cm long below them, the sacs densely furry, green then brown. The model's small cream ovals on stalks are the right place and nothing of the size or colour.

Carex praticola.note: Photographs: a loose tuft of narrow leaves with slender arching stems ending in a nodding string of a few silvery-green to brown oval spikes. Model: a bright yellow-green tuft with many pale flat ovals on upright stalks, more like an oat grass; the nodding string of spikes is missing.

earlier.note: A tufted sedge with slender stems that arch at the top, the head a loose, nodding string of 3 to 7 pale, silvery-green to straw oval spikelets, each narrowed at the base. The model's ovals stand upright on sticks beside wide dark straps. Six photographs, none of the whole plant.

Carex pseudocyperus.note: Photographs: a lush yellow-green tussock with several fat, bristly, cylindrical spikes hanging from thread-like stalks like bottle brushes. Model: a yellow-green tussock with small erect oval spikes on the stem tips; the colour and tuft are right, but the drooping bristly brushes that name it are missing.

earlier.note: Bright yellow-green, wide leaves and stems from which three to five thick, bristly, bottle-brush cylinders 3 to 6 cm long hang on thin stalks, green then brown. The hanging brushes are how it is known. The model has small cream ovals standing upright on sticks over dark straps.

Carex retrorsa.note: Photographs: a lush yellow-green tussock with several fat, bristly, star-like spikes crowded at the top of each stem among long leafy bracts. Model: a yellow-green tussock with smooth pointed ovals strung up tall stalks; the tussock and colour are right, but the heads are smooth and spread out where the plant's are fat, spiky and bunched among the leaves.

earlier.note: Wide, bright yellow-green leaves much longer than the stems, and three to six fat, spiky, green-yellow burs 3 to 5 cm long crowded together near the stem top, their beaked sacs bent backward. The model's small cream ovals do not read as spiky burs, and the body is dark.

Carex rostrata.note: Photographs: a sedge of wet ground with grey-green leaves and several erect, thick, cylindrical yellow-green spikes, bristly with beaked seeds. Model: a clump of blue-grey blades with small tan ovals clustered at the stem tips; the heads read as a grass's and the blades are bluer than the plant.

earlier.note: Narrow, blue-grey, channelled leaves and stems carrying two to four dense upright cylinders 3 to 8 cm long, yellow-green then straw, of round inflated sacs with sharp beaks. The model's small cream ovals on stalks are the right position, a fraction of the size, over dark green straps where the plant is blue-grey.

Carex sartwellii.note: Photographs: a spreading colony of upright leafy stems, each topped by a dense, elongated, many-spikeleted brown head that looks shaggy. Model: a colony of grassy leaves with smooth, dark brown, cigar-shaped heads on bare stalks; it reads as a sedge in seed, but the heads are smooth cattail-like ovals rather than shaggy clusters, and too dark.

earlier.note: A stiff sedge in stands, each stem ending in one narrow, dense, brown, cylindrical head 3 to 6 cm long made of many small spikes pressed together. The model's separate cream ovals on sticks over wide dark straps do not read as one brown head.

Carex sprengelii.note: Photographs: a lush tuft of soft, arching leaves with slender stems carrying a few short, plump spikes of round seeds that hang or nod on thin stalks. Model: a tuft with stiff upright stems ending in pale oval spikes; the tuft reads, but the spikes stand stiff and erect instead of nodding on threads.

earlier.note: A woodland sedge in arching clumps of narrow, soft, bright green leaves, with thin stems from which several pale green cylinders 2 to 3 cm long hang on thread-like stalks, each sac drawn out into a long beak. The model's ovals stand upright on sticks over stiff dark straps: nothing arches or hangs.

Carex utriculata.note: Photographs: a dense, tall stand of broad, yellow-green leaves with several thick, bristly, cylindrical spikes per stem, green then orange-brown. Model: a broad clump of yellow-green blades with slim, smooth orange ovals on bare stalks above them; the stand reads, but the spikes are thin smooth ovals instead of fat bristly cylinders among the leaves.

earlier.note: Stands of stout stems with wide yellow-green leaves, each stem with thin male spikes at the top and below them two to four thick, dense cylinders 4 to 10 cm long, straw-yellow to orange-brown, of inflated beaked sacs. No seed head is recorded, so the model draws yellow daisy shapes lying flat in a ring round a dark column.

Cerastium arvense.note: Photographs: a low, loose mat of narrow grey-green leafy stems with many white, deeply notched five-petalled flowers held a little above it. Model: a flat dark green octagonal plate on the ground ringed by sprigs, with tall thin stalks of white flowers standing round its edge; the flowers read, the body does not.

earlier.note: A loose mat of slender stems with pairs of small narrow grey-green leaves 1 to 2 cm, covered in white flowers 1.5 cm across, five petals each notched halfway, on thin stalks above the leaves. The model reads as a low plant with white flowers on top, close in kind. The leaves are long stiff blades and there are far fewer flowers than a plant in bloom carries.

Chamaenerion angustifolium.note: Photographs: a stand of single upright leafy stems with narrow leaves, ending in a long tapering spike of four-petalled magenta flowers, then silky seed. Model: a stand of tall leafy stems with pink flowers along their upper third; reads as fireweed. The pink is paler than the magenta in the photographs (the recorded colour, which is the owner's).

earlier.note: A tall unbranched stem crowded with willow-like leaves, ending in a long tapering spike of magenta four-petalled flowers 2 to 3 cm, buds drooping at the tip, long red seed pods below that split into white fluff. The model's leafy stems are right in kind. Its flowers are pale pink and dark maroon squares floating round the stem, where the plant is a solid magenta spire.

Cinna latifolia.note: Photographs: a woodland grass with broad flat leaves along its stems and a loose, nodding, open panicle. Model: a tufted grass with nodding open panicles above it; reads as the plant, though the blades are too fine and gathered at the base rather than broad along the stems.

earlier.note: A loose woodland grass with broad, flat, soft, bright green leaves spaced up the stem, and a large, open, drooping panicle 15 to 30 cm long whose fine branches hang to one side. The seed head is recorded nodding; the model shows almost none. The body is the same stiff column of dark straps as every grass.

Cirsium flodmanii.note: Photographs: a white-woolly, grey-green stem with deeply lobed spiny leaves and a few large magenta-purple thistle heads 3 to 4 cm over spiny green bracts. Model: a tall branched stem with cut leaves at the base and small purple heads at the tips; the outline is right, but it is green rather than woolly grey and the heads are too small.

earlier.note: A leafy thistle to a metre, the stem and leaf undersides white-woolly, the leaves deeply cut and spiny; each branch ends in a pink-purple brush 3 to 4 cm across on a spiny green urn. The model is a dark rosette of broad leaves under bare wires tipped with pink dots: not a thistle.

Clematis occidentalis.note: Photographs: a slender scrambling vine with three-part leaves, nodding blue-purple bells of four sepals in May, feathery silver seed heads after. Model: drawn on a host, the pair reads as one dense rounded shrub of feathery sprays with white specks; the vine cannot be told from what it climbs, and the seed heads are specks.

earlier.note: A slender woody vine with leaves of three pointed, heart-based leaflets 4 to 8 cm; nodding blue-violet lanterns of four long pointed sepals 4 to 6 cm; then silky feather-ball seed heads that last into winter. The model's vine is a few threads of tiny ladder leaves on the dogwood's side with flowers as specks in the air: the dogwood is all one sees. The sheet's camera frames the host, which makes a vine hard to judge.

Comandra umbellata.note: Photographs: a low, bushy colony of leafy stems with small, narrow, pale blue-green leaves crowding them to the top, and flat clusters of small white star flowers; small green-purple fruits later. Model: a colony of upright single stems with paired green leaves and small white flower clusters at the tips; the flowers read, but the stems stand too upright and sparse, and the leaves are green, not blue-grey.

earlier.note: Patches of slender upright stems a hand high, with small, pale blue-green, oblong leaves up the stem, and clusters of small white to pinkish star flowers at the top. The model's white flowers at the top are right. The body is a spiky ball of long bright green blades, like a small yucca; the leaf surface is recorded glaucous and the colour does not follow it.

Comarum palustre.note: Photographs: a sprawling, leafy plant of wet ground with grey-green leaves of five to seven toothed leaflets and star-shaped deep wine-red flowers with long pointed sepals. Model: two thin stems with small sparse fronds at the base and bright scarlet-orange flowers in loose sprays; the colour is far from the wine red (the recorded colour is the owner's) and the plant too thin and leafless.

earlier.note: Sprawling reddish stems in wet ground; blue-green leaves of 5 to 7 toothed, oblong leaflets, the upper ones set like fingers; flowers 2 cm, a star of five pointed wine-red sepals round a dark red centre. It is recorded orange-red; every photograph is deep wine red. The model's cloud of orange and near-black flecks hovers above an upright ladder-leaf stem.

Coreopsis tinctoria.note: Photographs: an airy, much-branched plant with fine thread-cut leaves and many yellow daisies with a dark red ring and centre, 2 to 4 cm. Model: a thin branched plant with small yellow and red heads scattered over it; the colours and airy habit read, but the heads are too small and the plant has almost no visible leaves.

earlier.note: A slender, much-branched plant with leaves cut into thread-like segments, and many heads 3 to 4 cm: eight broad, notched yellow rays, each with a maroon base, round a dark red-brown button. The model is a thin leafy stem with a few small dark discs lying flat, the yellow rays hardly showing.

Cornus canadensis.note: Photographs: a low carpet, each shoot a whorl of four to six veined leaves close to the ground with one white four-bracted flower in the centre, red berries in a tight cluster later. Model: a colony of shoots with leaf whorls and a white flower each, which reads as bunchberry; but the shoots stand on long bare stalks far above the ground, and each flower is a flat white square card.

earlier.note: A carpet of separate upright stems a hand high, each ending in one whorl of 4 to 6 pointed oval leaves with curved veins, and above it one flower of four broad white bracts 2 to 3 cm across round a green button; then a tight bunch of bright red berries in the centre of each whorl. The model is one mound of stacked plates with a pile of white confetti on top; its red berry bunches are close.

Cornus sericea.note: Photographs: a spreading shrub of red stems with opposite, smooth-edged oval leaves with curved veins, flat clusters of white flowers and then white berries; bright red twigs in winter. Model: a crown of paired leaves arranged into feather-like fronds on a clump of red stems, with small white flower clusters; the red stems are there, but the opposite leaves read as pinnate fronds, the stems form a bare red cage under the crown instead of being leafy, and no white berries show in August.

earlier.note: Many slender bright red stems, opposite oval leaves with curved veins, flat white clusters 4 to 5 cm across at the branch tips, white berries. The model has the red, on trunks as thick as an arm; the leaves are big plates in tiers; the flowers are specks floating above the shrub, and the berries do not show.

Corylus cornuta.note: Photographs: a many-stemmed open shrub with bright green, broad, coarsely toothed oval leaves, and in July paired bristly green husks drawn out into a beak. Model: a dense rounded shrub of small dark oval leaves in feather-like sprays; it could be any shrub. The leaves read too small and too dark, and no husks are drawn.

earlier.note: A dense many-stemmed shrub of slender stems; bright green oval leaves, doubly toothed, 5 to 10 cm; hanging yellow catkins on bare twigs in April; nuts in a long-beaked bristly husk. The model is thick sticks carrying big leaf plates in tiers, and bare sticks in April.

Crataegus chrysocarpa.note: Photographs: a thorny, many-stemmed large shrub to small tree with a dense, rounded crown of toothed oval leaves, flat clusters of white flowers in May and red haws in August. Model: a multi-stemmed shrub with a full, irregular crown of round leaves; the shape reads, but the May picture shows no white flowers and the August one no red haws, which are what tell it from the other big shrubs.

earlier.note: A dense, thorny, twiggy small tree; broad roundish leaves, sharply toothed and shallowly lobed; clusters of white five-petalled flowers in May; red haws. The model is a few thick forked trunks with leaf cards at the ends, no flower in May and no haws in August.

Cypripedium parviflorum.note: Photographs: a clump of leafy stems with broad, pleated, oval leaves, each topped by one flower: a yellow pouch with twisted maroon-brown petals either side. Model: a clump of leafy stems with broad leaves and a small flat yellow card at each tip; the leafy clump reads, but the pouch and twisted petals that make the orchid are a flat petal, and too small.

earlier.note: One stem with 3 to 5 pleated, strongly veined leaves that sheathe it and point up, and at the top one flower: a yellow pouch 3 to 5 cm with twisted maroon-brown ribbons either side. The model is a pagoda of dozens of leaf plates with small flat yellow discs lying on top.

Dalea purpurea.note: Photographs: a clump of wiry stems with small finely divided leaves, each topped by a dense thimble-shaped head with a ring of bright purple-magenta flowers and orange anthers. Model: a clump of long thin stems with loose open strings of lilac specks; the dense purple thimbles that make the plant are open strings, and the leaves are too small to show.

earlier.note: Several slender stems with leaves of 3 to 5 thread-narrow leaflets, each stem ending in a dense thimble 1 to 5 cm long and 1 cm thick: a ring of bright magenta flowers with orange anthers climbing a grey cone. The model's slender stems and small leaves are right. Its flowers are long open strings of dark violet dots, where the plant's is one solid thimble a stem.

Dasiphora fruticosa.note: Photographs: a dense, rounded shrub of fine grey-green leaves of five small leaflets, dotted all summer with flat bright yellow five-petalled flowers 2 to 3 cm. Model: a dense, rounded mound of fine leaves with yellow flowers round its edge; reads as shrubby cinquefoil, but each flower is a ragged yellow card rather than a flat round five-petalled cup, and the green is too dark and not grey.

earlier.note: A dense, rounded, fine-textured bush; small grey-green leaves of five narrow leaflets; yellow five-petalled flowers 2 to 3 cm scattered over the whole bush all summer; shredding red-brown bark. The model has the yellow flowers at their size, all in a flat cap above a sparse V of sticks.

Doellingeria umbellata.note: Photographs: a tall leafy plant with lance leaves up the stems, ending in a broad flat-topped cluster of white daisies about 2 cm with yellow centres. Model: tall leafy stems with a small flat cluster of white specks at the top; the plant reads, but the daisies are too small to read as daisies and the cluster too sparse.

earlier.note: Tall leafy stems, lance leaves 8 to 15 cm, topped by a broad flat-topped cluster 10 to 30 cm across of many small white daisies with 7 to 14 rays and yellow centres. The model's leafy stems are right in kind; in August, mid-flowering, it shows no flowers at all.

Drosera rotundifolia.note: Photographs: a tiny rosette of round leaf blades on stalks, red and covered in glistening sticky hairs, in moss, with a thin stalk of small white flowers. Model: a tiny green rosette with one thin stalk; the red glistening leaves, the plant's whole identity, are plain green.

earlier.note: A rosette 3 to 8 cm across of round leaves on flat stalks, red and fringed with sticky glistening hairs, flat on the moss; one thin stalk with a few small white flowers down one side. The model is a few hair-thin lines: no rosette, no red. A plant this small may be beyond what a yard view can show, but a red rosette is drawable.

Drymocallis arguta.note: Photographs: a stiff, hairy, upright plant with large pinnate basal leaves and a narrow, crowded cluster of creamy white to pale yellow five-petalled flowers at the top. Model: thin bare stalks with a few small fronds at the base and loose sprays of small bright yellow flowers; the flowers read bright yellow rather than cream (the recorded colour is the owner's), and the leafy base is far too sparse.

earlier.note: Stiff, upright, sticky-hairy stems from a tuft of basal leaves; leaves of 7 to 11 toothed leaflets; a tight flat cluster at the top of cream to pale yellow flowers 1.5 cm. The model's upright stems and top cluster are right in kind; the cluster is a flat cloud of yellow and near-black flecks, and the leaflets are plain ovals.

Elaeagnus commutata.note: Photographs: an upright suckering shrub of brown stems with broad, bright silvery leaves, small fragrant yellow tubular flowers in June among the leaves, then dry silvery berries held into winter. Model: an open thicket of thin stems with silvery-green oval leaves; the silver reads well, but it stands as a loose grove of separate sticks, the June picture shows no flowers and there are no silver berries.

earlier.note: Upright stems with brown scurfy twigs, silver leaves on both sides, small yellow flowers tucked in the leaf axils in June, silvery mealy berries that stay into winter. The model has the silver. It is a sparse V of brown trunks, and since no flower shape is recorded it never flowers; its berries do not show.

Eleocharis acicularis.note: Photographs: a dense, low carpet of hair-fine bright green stems, often under shallow water, with tiny brown spikelets at the tips. Model: a small clump of thin upright stems with brown tips; right in kind, but too stiff and sparse for what is a mat-forming turf, and darker green.

earlier.note: A low, bright green turf of hair-fine stems 5 to 15 cm tall, like a lawn of green threads, each tipped with a tiny spikelet a few millimetres long. The model is one tall narrow column of blades with tan blocks as big as the plant floating beside it. It is the smallest plant drawn with the largest seed head.

Eleocharis palustris.note: Photographs: a dense stand of thin, leafless green stems, each tipped with a small brown spikelet, pale and cream while in flower. Model: thin upright green stems with small dark tips; reads as a spikerush. The stand is thinner than in the photographs.

earlier.note: Stands of thin, round, leafless, bright green stems like knitting needles, each tipped with one small pointed brown spikelet 1 to 2 cm long, cream when in flower. It is recorded with a red flower colour. The model is a tussock of wide flat straps with large bright red blocks on stalks: wrong body, wrong head, wrong colour.

Elymus canadensis.note: Photographs: a loose bunch of blue-green leafy stems with long, nodding, bristly spikes with curving awns. Model: a tussock with pale arching spikes above it; it reads as a wild rye, but the spikes stand too stiffly and the long awns that make it bristly do not show.

earlier.note: A loose tuft of broad blue-green leaves, with stems to 1.2 m each ending in a thick, bristly spike 10 to 25 cm long that arches over and nods, its long awns curving outward, like a bearded rye. The model is a narrow dark column of stiff straps with one small pale upright block: the big nodding bristly head is the plant's whole character.

Elymus trachycaulus.note: Photographs: an upright, narrow bunchgrass with slender stiff stems and narrow, flat spikes of overlapping spikelets, green then straw. Model: a narrow upright tussock with thin spikes above it; reads as a wheatgrass. The blades are a darker blue-green than the plant's green.

earlier.note: A loose upright tuft of flat blue-green leaves, with many stiff stems each ending in a very slender, straight spike 8 to 20 cm long, the spikelets pressed flat against it in two rows. The model's narrow upright column suits it better than most grasses; its heads are short tan blocks where the plant's are long and pencil-thin.

Equisetum arvense.note: Photographs: a patch of green jointed stems with whorls of thin green branches, like small bottlebrushes, and pale fertile stems with a brown cone in spring. Model: jointed green stems with whorled branches; reads as the plant. A little stiff and evenly spaced.

earlier.note: Bright green jointed stems with whorls of slender green branches at every joint, the branches angled upward and often branching again, so the plant is a soft bottle-brush; in spring, separate pale brown stems with a cone. The model reads as a horsetail at once. The real plant's branches are longer, finer and more crowded, and its stems thinner.

Equisetum fluviatile.note: Photographs: a dense stand of tall, smooth, hollow green stems, some with short whorls of branches at the middle joints, some bearing a small cone at the tip. Model: a stand of tall jointed stems with short whorled branches; reads as swamp horsetail. The green is too dark and blue for its fresh bright green.

earlier.note: Stands of tall, smooth, hollow, bright green stems in shallow water, many with no branches at all and others with short irregular whorls in the middle; a dark cone at the tip of some. The model does the job: thin jointed stems with whorls in the middle. It is darker than the plant's light green.

Equisetum hyemale.note: Photographs: stiff, unbranched, dark green jointed stems with black and pale bands at each joint and a small pointed cone at the tip. Model: jointed banded stems with pointed tips; reads as scouring-rush.

earlier.note: Stiff, unbranched, dark evergreen stems, jointed, each joint ringed by a pale sheath with black bands, ending in a small pointed cone. The model does the job: unbranched jointed stems with dark rings and pointed tips, in a loose stand. Its rings are all black where the plant's are ash-grey between two black lines. Four photographs.

Equisetum variegatum.note: Photographs: a low, dense tuft of very thin, dark green, evergreen stems, banded black and white at the joints, a few centimetres to 30 cm, each with a tiny pointed cone. Model: jointed, banded stems with pointed tips; it reads as a horsetail, but the stems are thick and leaning, more like a scouring-rush, where this one is wiry and fine.

earlier.note: As the Scouring-rush in miniature: thin, wiry, unbranched evergreen stems 10 to 35 cm tall in loose tufts, the sheath teeth black with white edges, a small pointed cone at the tip. The model reads as a small horsetail. Its stems are too thick for their height, and lean out more than the plant's do.

Erigeron glabellus.note: Photographs: a basal clump of spoon leaves under leafy stems with a few lilac-pink daisies 3 cm with hundreds of fine rays round a yellow centre, facing out and up. Model: a basal clump and tall stems with small yellow and pink specks at the tips; the daisies are seen edge-on and read as dots, so it does not read as a fleabane.

earlier.note: A tuft of narrow spoon leaves, a few smaller leaves up each stem, and one to three daisies per stem, 2 to 3 cm, with a hundred or more narrow lilac, pink or white rays round a yellow centre. The model's heads face straight up, so from the side they are specks in the air above bare wires.

Erigeron philadelphicus.note: Photographs: a basal rosette of soft leaves under branched stems topped by many small daisies 1.5 to 2.5 cm with hundreds of thread-like pale pink to white rays round a yellow centre. Model: a leaf rosette and thin branched stems with a few tiny pinkish-yellow dots; the daisies are too small and too few to read.

earlier.note: A rosette of soft spoon-shaped leaves and a hairy stem with clasping leaves, branching at the top into ten to thirty daisies 1.5 to 2.5 cm: a hundred or more thread-thin white to pale pink rays round a yellow centre. The model has the rosette, then bare wires and a few orange-brown specks in the air.

Eriophorum angustifolium.note: Photographs: a sedge of wet ground with narrow leaves and stems carrying a few nodding, drooping heads that become soft white cotton tufts, hanging loosely. Model: a grassy clump with large white faceted balls on stalks; the white heads make it read as cotton-grass, but they are hard polyhedra standing upright rather than soft drooping tufts, and too big.

earlier.note: Slender stems in open bog, each hanging two to seven tufts of long, pure white, silky cotton 3 to 4 cm, which is the plant: white-flecked bog from a distance. The seed head is recorded bristly, so the model draws the needle-grass's flat fan of rays, tan, beside wide dark straps. The cotton shows in June and July, after its recorded May flowering.

Eurybia conspicua.note: Photographs: a leafy plant with large broad ovate leaves up the stem, topped by a flat cluster of violet daisies 3 to 4 cm with yellow centres. Model: leafy stems with broad leaves, topped by small yellow-centred heads whose violet rays barely show; the leaves are right, but the flowers read as yellow buttons.

earlier.note: Large, rough, toothed oval leaves mostly on the lower stem, and an open flat-topped cluster above them of violet daisies 3 to 4 cm with yellow centres. The model is a solid cone of leaf plates to the top, like a pine cone, with a few specks.

Eurybia sibirica.note: Photographs: a low, sprawling to ascending plant on gravel, leafy stems, lilac-purple daisies about 3 cm with yellow centres. Model: an upright clump of leafy stems with a few small lilac heads on top; the colour and leaves are right, the plant stands too straight and the heads are too small and too few.

earlier.note: A low spreading plant of leafy stems, lance to oval leaves 3 to 6 cm, each stem ending in one to a few lilac daisies 3 cm across with yellow centres. Recorded with 12 cm leaves on a 40 cm plant, so the model is a pagoda of leaf plates each a third of the plant wide, with a few specks on top.

Euthamia graminifolia.note: Photographs: a bushy, branched plant crowded with narrow grass-like leaves, ending in a flat-topped cluster of small golden heads. Model: bare thin branched stems with a few tiny leaves, holding open flat sprays of yellow dots; the flat top is there, but the plant is a bare skeleton where it is densely leafy and the heads are specks.

earlier.note: A bushy plant branching in its upper half, with many narrow grass-like leaves 4 to 8 cm, each branch ending in a small dense cluster of yellow so the top is one broad flat plate of gold. The model has the narrow leaves, drawn large and stiff; its flat top is a faint line of specks.

Eutrochium maculatum.note: Photographs: tall leafy purple-spotted stems with whorls of large toothed leaves, topped by big domed clusters of dusty pink flowers. Model: a few thin stems with whorls of narrow leaves and nothing on top; the flower domes that make the plant are not drawn in its flowering month.

earlier.note: A stout purple or purple-spotted stem to 1.5 m with whorls of 4 or 5 toothed lance leaves, topped by a broad, flat to domed head 10 to 20 cm across of fuzzy pink-purple. The model's whorled leaves up a tall stem are the right kind, the best whorled body so far; in August it shows no flower at all, and the leaves are thin blades.

Festuca hallii.note: Photographs: a dense tussock of fine, rough, grey-green leaves with slender, open, few-branched panicles of narrow spikelets that are purplish then straw. Model: a fine pale tussock (right) under thick, heavy, pinkish-brown zigzag club heads; the heads are much too thick and dense for this fescue's slim panicles.

earlier.note: A large dense tussock of stiff, rough, grey-green rolled leaves 20 to 30 cm long, with stems to 60 cm carrying narrow panicles of purplish spikelets. The model is the dark column of wide straps with tan blocks. Only four photographs and none of a whole tussock, so the body cannot be judged from the sheet.

Festuca saximontana.note: Photographs: a small, dense, fine-leaved bluish tuft with very narrow, few-branched straw-coloured panicles on thin stems. Model: a blue-green tuft with dense, heavy, purple club-like heads; the tuft is right, but the heads are far too thick and too purple for this fine fescue.

earlier.note: A small dense cushion of hair-fine, blue-grey leaves 5 to 10 cm tall, with many thin stems to 30 cm carrying narrow panicles 3 to 8 cm long, purplish then straw. The model's tuft with heads above it is right in kind; its leaves are wide flat straps and its heads are fat tan blocks. Six photographs.

Fragaria vesca.note: Photographs: a low rosette of bright green, three-part, sharply toothed leaves with white flowers and small, bright red, pointed berries held up above the leaves. Model: a low rosette of three-part leaves with white flowers above; reads as woodland strawberry. The July fruit is a few red specks rather than small strawberries.

earlier.note: As Wild Strawberry, with thinner, brighter green, strongly veined leaflets whose end tooth is longer than its neighbours, and a pointed berry held above the leaves with its seeds on the surface. The model is the same as Wild Strawberry's, which is fair: little that is recorded tells them apart.

Fragaria virginiana.note: Photographs: a low rosette of three-part, toothed, blue-green leaves on hairy stalks, red runners, and white five-petalled flowers with yellow centres just above the leaves, then small red strawberries hanging below. Model: a rosette of three-part leaves with white flowers above; reads as a wild strawberry. The June fruit is tiny red specks among the flowers rather than strawberries hanging on stalks.

earlier.note: Tufts of long-stalked leaves, each of three broad, coarsely toothed, blue-green leaflets, joined by red runners; white five-petalled flowers 1.5 to 2 cm with a yellow centre, held about level with the leaves; small red strawberries hanging below. The model reads as a strawberry in flower. The leaflets are narrow rather than broad and toothed, and the berries sit out at the edge of the plant.

Gaillardia aristata.note: Photographs: a leafy clump with heads 5 to 7 cm, yellow rays with a red base around a dark red domed centre, on stems not much above the leaves. Model: tall bare stems far above a low leaf clump, each topped by a flat orange-red head; too leggy, and the head reads orange (the recorded colour, which is the owner's) rather than yellow with a red ring.

earlier.note: A clump of leafy stems, grey-green and hairy, the leaves running up the lower stem; heads 5 to 7 cm with yellow rays, red at the base, three-toothed at the tip, round a red-brown dome; a round seed ball after. The model is a flat near-black rosette with bare wire stalks and dark red discs hovering above their tips: the rays read dark orange, not yellow.

Galium boreale.note: Photographs: a dense leafy clump of square stems with whorls of four narrow leaves, topped by a foamy mass of tiny white flowers in branched clusters. Model: a sparse bundle of bare straight stems with a scatter of white specks floating around them; no leaf whorls show and no white foam.

earlier.note: A dense patch of many upright square stems, each ringed every few centimetres with a whorl of four narrow three-veined leaves 2 to 4 cm, topped with frothy pyramids of tiny white flowers. It is recorded sprawling; it stands up. The model is a ring of specks on the ground, three bare hairs and a ball of dots in the air.

Galium triflorum.note: Photographs: a low, trailing woodland plant of weak stems with whorls of five or six bright green elliptic leaves, and tiny greenish-white flowers in threes on thin stalks. Model: a flat green octagonal plate with sprigs round its edge and tall bare stalks hung with white specks; nothing of the trailing whorled stems.

earlier.note: Weak trailing stems with whorls of six bright green leaves, widest above the middle and tipped with a point, like spokes of a wheel, spaced along the stem; tiny greenish-white flowers in threes; small bristly burs. The model is a dense starburst of long blades from one point with white specks: none of the neat spaced wheels of six.

Gentianella amarella.note: Photographs: a small upright plant with paired leaves and many narrow, tubular lilac to violet flowers crowded up the stem in the leaf joints. Model: two leafy stems with open pink stars at a few joints and at the top; the habit is right, but the colour reads pink rather than lilac-violet (the recorded colour is the owner's), the flowers are open stars instead of narrow tubes, and there are too few.

earlier.note: A small stiff plant with opposite lance leaves, and narrow upright tubes 1 to 2 cm long that open into 4 or 5 small pointed lobes, lilac to violet, bunched in the leaf axils all the way up the stem. It is recorded pink and 2 cm across. The model is a tuft of long blades under large flat pink and near-black plates.

Geranium richardsonii.note: Photographs: a leafy clump of deeply cut, hand-shaped leaves under branching stems of white five-petalled flowers with fine purple veins. Model: a clump of palmate leaves under branched stems with white five-petalled flowers; reads as a white geranium. The basal leaves are a little sparse for the plant's leafy clump.

earlier.note: An open bushy plant of long-stalked leaves cut into 5 to 7 sharp-toothed fingers, red in autumn; white flowers 2.5 to 3 cm with five rounded petals lined in purple, in pairs above the leaves. The model's white flowers are the right size and read well; the leaves are plain ovals in a stack, and the flowers bunch in one cloud at the top.

Geum aleppicum.note: Photographs: a leafy, hairy, branching plant with large pinnate basal leaves and three-lobed stem leaves, bright yellow buttercup flowers 1.5 to 2 cm, and round bristly seed burs. Model: a few thin branched stems with small yellow flowers over a faint skirt of tiny fronds; the flowers read, but the leafy body and the burs are missing.

earlier.note: A leafy, hairy, branching stem to a metre; leaves of sharply toothed leaflets with a large wedge-shaped end one; yellow five-petalled flowers 1.5 to 2 cm at the branch tips; round bristly bur heads. The model is a small ladder-leaf rosette under a bundle of bare wires with a thin scatter of flowers above.

Geum macrophyllum.note: Photographs: a clump of large basal leaves with a big round lobed end leaflet, under leafy branching stems with small yellow buttercup-like flowers and round bristly seed heads. Model: a few thin branched stems with small yellow flowers over a sparse skirt of small pinnate fronds; the big round leaves that name it are missing.

earlier.note: Basal leaves with a very large round, lobed end leaflet and a few small ones below it; leafy branching stems with three-lobed leaves; yellow five-petalled flowers 1.5 cm; round bur heads of hooked seeds. The model's leaves are ladders of small equal leaflets, near black; the stalks are bare wires and the flowers a pale cloud above them.

Geum rivale.note: Photographs: a clump of large pinnate basal leaves with a big end leaflet, under hairy purple stems with nodding bell-like flowers of dusky purple sepals and cream-pink petals, then bristly seed heads. Model: thin branched stems over small sparse fronds, with flat upturned lilac stars; the nodding purple bells, which make it water avens, are not there.

earlier.note: Nodding bells on arching hairy stalks: a dusky purple-maroon cup round cream to pink petals; basal leaves with a big rounded end leaflet; bristly seed heads. The model is one tall stalk under a flat cloud of pale lilac and black stars, with ladder leaves.

Geum triflorum.note: Photographs: a low rosette of soft, finely cut, fern-like grey-green leaves under short stalks of nodding dusty-pink to maroon bell flowers in threes, then pink feathery plumes. Model: a sparse ring of pinnate fronds under tall bare stalks with small upturned pale pink stars; the nodding maroon bells and the feathery plumes, which make prairie smoke, are not there.

earlier.note: A rosette of ferny leaves, many toothed leaflets growing larger toward the tip; several reddish stalks each with three nodding, closed, dusky rose-pink urns; then long feathery pink plumes, the smoke it is named for. The model's rosette is the right kind. It has one stalk, open stars facing sideways, and no plumes.

Glyceria grandis.note: Photographs: a tall, leafy wet-ground grass with broad flat leaves and a large, open, drooping, purplish panicle. Model: a narrow tuft of fine blades with thin stems and small open panicles at the top; it reads as a grass, but too thin in leaf and too small in head for this one.

earlier.note: A stout wetland grass with broad flat leaves, topped by a very large, open, much-branched panicle 20 to 40 cm long and nearly as wide, its many small spikelets purple, nodding at the ends of fine branches. The seed head is recorded correctly as an open panicle; the model shows a faint speck at the top of a narrow column of straps.

Glyceria striata.note: Photographs: a soft, leafy wet-ground grass with an open, nodding panicle of tiny purplish spikelets on fine drooping branches. Model: a yellow-green tussock with fine open panicles on tall stems; it reads as a soft grass, but the panicles stand upright instead of nodding and the tuft is yellower than the plant.

earlier.note: A slender wetland grass in loose tufts, with an open panicle 10 to 20 cm long of drooping thread-fine branches beaded with small oval spikelets, green then purple. The model's pale beaded heads are the right idea and the best seed head of the grasses so far; they stand stiffly upright where the plant's droop, on the same column of wide straps.

Glycyrrhiza lepidota.note: Photographs: a dense, leafy colony of stems clothed in large pinnate leaves of many narrow leaflets, with short, dense, cream flower spikes, then clusters of brown burs covered in hooked prickles. Model: three tall bare stems with a skirt of small fronds at the base and a loose spray of white specks above; neither the leafy stems, nor the dense spikes, nor the burs read.

earlier.note: A bushy plant with leaves of 11 to 19 lance leaflets; dense upright spikes of cream pea flowers, shorter than the leaves; then clusters of rust-brown burs covered in hooked prickles that stay on the dead stems all winter. The model's ladder leaves are right. It is one stem with pale dots scattered round its top, and no burs.

Grindelia squarrosa.note: Photographs: a rounded, bushy, much-branched plant of grey-green toothed leaves covered in yellow daisies 2 to 3 cm with sticky curled bracts. Model: an open spray of thin stems with small yellow heads, more like a branched aster; it should be a dense, rounded, leafy bush, and the heads are too small.

earlier.note: A rounded bushy plant, much branched, with small toothed oblong leaves and dozens of bright yellow daisies 2.5 to 3.5 cm, each on a green bur of curled-back sticky bracts. The model is a few thin stems with long grass blades and five or six small orange specks.

Hedysarum americanum.note: Photographs: a bushy, leafy clump with pinnate leaves of many leaflets, each stem ending in a long one-sided raceme of drooping pink-purple pea flowers. Model: about ten nearly bare stalks with a few small pinnate leaves near the ground and pink flecks strung loosely up every stalk; no dense raceme, and the clump is a broom, not a bush.

earlier.note: A bushy clump of leafy stems, leaves of 9 to 21 leaflets, each stem ending in a long, slim, one-sided raceme of drooping pink-purple pea flowers; flat pods pinched into round links. The model's pinnate leaves read well. It is one stem, and its flowers are a cloud of pink flecks spread across the whole plant, not on spikes.

Hedysarum boreale.note: Photographs: a bushy, leafy clump of grey-green pinnate leaves with dense racemes of vivid magenta pea flowers. Model: an upright broom of bare stalks with pale pink flecks strung up them and a thin skirt of leaves at the base; no leafy bush and no dense racemes, and the pink is far paler than the magenta (the recorded colour is the owner's).

earlier.note: A bushy clump of many stems with grey-green leaves of 9 to 15 narrow leaflets; racemes of bright magenta to red-purple pea flowers 1.5 to 2 cm; pods of flat round joints. It is recorded pale pink. The model is one stem of ladder leaves with pale pink flecks scattered round it.

Helenium autumnale.note: Photographs: a leafy, branched clump with many yellow daisies 3 to 5 cm, each with fan-shaped, three-toothed, drooping rays round a round yellow ball centre. Model: a clump of thin leafy stems with small yellow heads at the tips; the colour is right but the heads, seen mostly edge-on, are too small to show their ball centres and drooping rays.

earlier.note: Leafy winged stems branching at the top into many heads 3 to 5 cm: wedge-shaped yellow rays with three teeth, bent back round a yellow to green-yellow ball 1 to 2 cm across. The centre is recorded brown; it is yellow. The model in September is an olive-brown stem with a few tiny dark discs.

Helianthus nuttallii.note: Photographs: tall, leafy, branched stems with long narrow leaves and many bright yellow sunflowers 5 to 7 cm with brown centres. Model: a tall, narrow bundle of stems with small tan and yellow heads on top; the heads are too small to read as sunflowers and the stems carry too few leaves.

earlier.note: Tall slender stems to 2 m, narrow lance leaves 8 to 15 cm, several sunflowers 5 to 8 cm with yellow rays round a yellow-brown centre. The model's tall leafy stems are right in kind; its leaves are broad paddles, and the heads are small dark discs in the air above the plant with no yellow showing.

Helianthus pauciflorus.note: Photographs: stiff, rough, grey-green stems with paired thick lance leaves and a few large yellow sunflowers 6 to 8 cm with dark purple-brown centres.
