Model: a colony of tall stiff single stems with paired leaves and a few yellow-and-brown heads at the tips; it reads as a prairie sunflower, but the heads are small for their 7 cm, the leaves too few and plain green.

earlier.note: Slender stiff stems, few and rough lance leaves mostly on the lower half, the upper stem nearly bare, each ending in a sunflower 6 to 8 cm with yellow rays round a dark red-brown disc. The model is a dense column of huge overlapping leaves, like a tobacco plant, with small dark heads buried in it.

Hesperostipa comata.note: Photographs: a fine-leaved bunchgrass with long, thread-like, curling awns trailing from the seeds, the heads loose and silvery straw in early summer. Model: a fine tussock with pale, airy, thread-like heads above it; reads as needle-and-thread. The long curling awns are straight and stiff rather than looping and trailing.

earlier.note: A dense bunch of fine, rolled, grey-green leaves, with stems whose seeds each trail a thread-thin awn 10 to 15 cm long, straight then curling and tangling, so the heads shimmer silver in wind. The model's bristly head is a flat fan of rays on a stick, like a dandelion clock, beside a spray of wide dark straps.

Hesperostipa curtiseta.note: Photographs (few): a tufted grass with narrow leaves and loose nodding heads of seeds with long, bent, twisted awns. Model: a tussock with pale airy heads above it; it reads as a needlegrass, but the bent awns are fine straight threads.

earlier.note: A bunchgrass of fine rolled leaves with long, bent, thread-like awns, shorter than Porcupine Grass's. The model is the same wide straps and flat dandelion-clock fans. Only four photographs and one is a thistle with the grass behind it, so little can be judged from the sheet.

Hesperostipa spartea.note: Photographs: a tall, coarse bunchgrass with long flat leaves and loose nodding heads of large seeds with very long, twisted, bent awns. Model: a tussock with loose pale airy heads above it; it reads as a needlegrass, but the long bent awns, which give it its look, are fine straight threads, and the blades are too narrow.

earlier.note: A tall bunchgrass with long narrow leaves and nodding stems whose few large seeds each carry a stout awn 12 to 20 cm long, twisted below and bent twice, hanging like quills. The model draws the same flat dandelion-clock fans as Needle and Thread.

Heterotheca villosa.note: Photographs: a low, bushy, spreading clump of hairy grey-green leafy stems covered in bright yellow daisies 2 to 3 cm. Model: an open spray of tall thin green stems with yellow heads at the top; it should be a low, leafy, grey mound, not a broom of bare green stems.

earlier.note: A low grey-hairy clump of many leafy stems, small oblong grey-green leaves 2 to 4 cm, and many bright yellow daisies 2 to 3 cm. The model is tall thin stems with long green grass blades; its heads are small and dark from the side.

Heuchera richardsonii.note: Photographs: a basal clump of rounded, shallowly lobed and scalloped leaves under tall leafless stalks with a narrow panicle of small greenish-cream bells. Model: two rosettes of sharp star-shaped leaves under tall bare stalks with red specks round their tops; the stalks are right, the leaves too sharply lobed, and the flowers drawn red (the recorded colour, which the photographs do not show).

earlier.note: A rosette of round, scalloped, shallowly lobed leaves and a few tall bare hairy stalks, each ending in a narrow spike of small greenish-yellow to tan bells. The model's rosette and bare stalks are the right kind. Its flowers are red stars scattered in a cloud off the stalks: every photograph shows green-yellow, and they sit on the stalk.

Hieracium umbellatum.note: Photographs: leafy upright stems with narrow toothed leaves and a flat-topped spray of several bright yellow dandelion-like heads 2 to 3 cm at the top. Model: leafy stems with a few small yellow dots at the tips; the habit is right but the heads are too small and too few to read as hawkweed.

earlier.note: A leafy stem, narrow toothed lance leaves crowded all the way up and no rosette at flowering, branching at the top into a loose cluster of yellow dandelion-like heads 2 to 3 cm; a tan pappus ball after. The model is a hand-sized rosette under bare wires with a few yellow specks: nothing of the plant.

Hippuris vulgaris.note: Photographs: unbranched upright stems standing out of shallow water, each a bottlebrush of short narrow leaves in close whorls. Model: upright stems with whorls of short leaves all the way up; reads as the plant. The green is darker and bluer than the bright yellow-green in the photographs.

earlier.note: Unbranched stems standing out of shallow water, closely ringed with whorls of 6 to 12 soft, narrow leaves 1 to 3 cm that curve upward, so each stem is a soft green bottle-brush tapering to the tip; yellow-green. The model reads as the plant: whorled upright stems. Its whorls are short stiff spikes set far apart on a thick dark stem, more like a bamboo cane.

Juncus balticus.note: Photographs: a dense, spreading colony of stiff, round, blue-green stems in rows from creeping roots, with a loose, branched cluster of small dark brown flowers sticking out from one side near the top. Model: a loose stand of thin green stems with boxy brown clusters partway up; the side-borne clusters read, but they are blocky cubes, and the stand is too sparse and green for this dense blue-green rush.

earlier.note: Straight rows of stiff, round, dark green, leafless stems rising from a creeping root, each with a loose spray of dark brown flowers bursting from one side a third of the way down from its sharp tip. The model is a tussock of wide flat straps with rust clusters on separate stalks: the plant is a row of wires, and its head is on the stem's side.

Juncus nodosus.note: Photographs: thin, upright, round stems and leaves with a few small, spiky, star-shaped brown heads on short branches at the top. Model: a grassy tuft with tall stalks of red-brown faceted heads; it reads as a rush in fruit, but the heads are boxy and too red, and the blades too broad and bright for round rush stems.

earlier.note: Thin, round, bright green stems and leaves, with several perfectly round, spiky, star-burst balls 1 cm across, red-brown, at the top. The model's rust-coloured clusters on stalks are the right colour and place, the best seed head of the rushes; they are loose dots rather than tight spiky balls, over wide flat straps.

Juncus vaseyi.note: Photographs (only two): stiff tufted stems with a small tight cluster of pale brown capsules at the tip. Model: a tussock with long stalks carrying orange faceted diamonds; the tussock is right, the heads are too orange, too big and too geometric, like lollipops.

earlier.note: A slender rush with thin round stems and a small tight cluster of straw to chestnut capsules at the top. The model's brown clusters at leaf height are fair; the body is wide flat straps where a rush is round wires. Only two photographs, both of the seed head, so the plant's form cannot be judged from the sheet.

Juniperus communis.note: Photographs: a dense, prickly, spreading mound of short sharp needles in whorls, grey-green to blue-green with a silvery band, turning bronze in winter, with dusty blue berries. Model: a loose mound of bright green feathery sprays that read as fern fronds; the colour is too warm and bright, the texture too soft, and no berries.

earlier.note: A dense evergreen mat or low spreading bush of sharp awl needles in threes, bright green with a white stripe, with blue-black berries. The model is bare brown sticks radiating from a point with dark slivers on them: a dead bush. Nothing of the green mass that is the whole plant.

Juniperus horizontalis.note: Photographs: a flat, spreading carpet of long trailing branches covered in short scale and awl leaves, blue-grey to grey-green, bronze-purple in winter, with dusty blue berries. Model: a flat starburst of broad plain green blades, like a small agave; nothing of a juniper.

earlier.note: A flat evergreen carpet of long trailing woody branches with feathery sprays of tiny scale leaves, blue-green to grey-green, purplish in winter, with blue-white berries. The model is a star of grass-like blades from one point, bright green: a tuft, not a woody mat. Only six photographs, none in flower since it has none.

Koeleria macrantha.note: Photographs: a low tuft of fine grey-green leaves with many narrow, dense, silvery-cream spike-like panicles standing above it. Model: a dark tuft with dense cream spikes held above it; reads as June grass. The leaves are much darker and greener than the plant's grey-green.

earlier.note: A small dense tuft of short, narrow, grey-green basal leaves a hand high, with many stiff bare stems to 50 cm each ending in a dense, narrow, silvery-green to pale gold spike 4 to 10 cm long that opens fluffy in flower. No seed head is recorded, so the model draws white daisies lying flat above a spray of long wide straps as tall as the stems.

Larix laricina.note: Photographs: an open, airy, narrow conifer with thin, irregular, often drooping branches and soft tufts of light green needles; small red cones in May; leafless in winter, gold in October. Model: a tight, dense, perfectly conical column of bright green foliage on a straight trunk; it reads as a spruce rather than an open tamarack, and the May picture shows no red cones.

earlier.note: An open, airy cone of slender level branches carrying soft tufts of light green needles; bare and twiggy in winter. The model's colour is right, but the crown is solid flat plates with the spruce's pencil tip: nothing of the tree's feathery, see-through look.

Lathyrus ochroleucus.note: Photographs: a sprawling, climbing herb about a metre long, with pinnate leaves of a few broad oval leaflets, tendrils, and short racemes of cream pea flowers. Model: drawn over a host shrub with red stems, the pair is one dense rounded shrub of pinnate fronds with white specks; the peavine cannot be seen as a plant of its own.

earlier.note: A climbing pea with leaves of 3 to 5 pairs of broad oval blue-green leaflets ending in a tendril, large leafy stipules, and one-sided racemes of 5 to 10 creamy yellow-white pea flowers 1.5 cm. The model's vine is a wisp of tiny leaves at the dogwood's foot with grey specks above the host.

Lathyrus venosus.note: Photographs: a climbing or sprawling vine with pinnate leaves of several oval leaflets and dense racemes of purple pea flowers. Model: drawn on a host with red stems, the pair is one dense, rounded shrub of pinnate fronds with white specks; the peavine is lost, and its purple flowers show as white.

earlier.note: A stout climbing pea with leaves of 4 to 6 pairs of oval, veined leaflets ending in a tendril, and dense one-sided racemes of 10 to 20 purple and pink pea flowers. The model's vine is a wisp at the dogwood's foot with flecks in the air above the host.

Ledum groenlandicum.note: Photographs: a low, open shrub of upright stems with narrow, leathery, dark green leaves rolled at the edges and rusty-woolly beneath, crowded at the stem tips, with round white clusters of small flowers on top. Model: a dense, bright green dome of fine leaves with white specks scattered over it; the leaves read too fresh and bright and the flowers are not in rounded clusters at the tips.

earlier.note: A low evergreen shrub; narrow leathery leaves with rolled edges, rusty wool beneath, drooping in winter; round white clusters 4 to 5 cm across at the shoot tips. The model's leaves are broad bright plates on a thick trunk and its flowers are white specks hovering above the bush.

Lemna trisulca.note: Photographs: a tangled, submerged mat of small, translucent, narrow-stalked fronds joined in chains at right angles, dark green to brownish, just under the surface. Model: a cluster of small round pale green pads floating on top of the water, like common duckweed; the branching chains and the submerged look are missing.

earlier.note: Thin, translucent, olive-green fronds 0.5 to 1 cm long, pointed and stalked, joined crosswise in chains and tangled mats that float just under the surface, not on it. The model is round green dots on the water, the common duckweed's look. At this size the difference hardly shows in a yard. Only four photographs.

Leymus innovatus.note: Photographs: a loose, spreading grass of open woods with blue-grey leaves and dense, soft, hairy spikes that are purplish then grey, often leaning. Model: a loose patch of blue-grey blades with stiff upright purplish spikes; it reads as a wild rye, but the spikes stand too straight and even, and the leaves are a little dark.

earlier.note: A stiff blue-green grass with rolled leaves and a dense, erect to slightly arching spike 5 to 12 cm long, grey-purple and visibly hairy. The model's pale upright blocks are the right position; they are flat tan rectangles, and the leaves are wide straps. Only six photographs, none of the whole plant in leaf.

Liatris ligulistylis.note: Photographs: an upright stem with narrow leaves and a short spike of large fluffy purple-magenta button heads, the top one largest, 2 to 3 cm. Model: two thin stems with narrow leaves and small pink stars spaced up their tops; the fuzzy purple buttons that make it a blazingstar are tiny pink stars instead, and the spike is too open.

earlier.note: An unbranched stem with narrow leaves that shrink upward, carrying a few to a dozen round shaggy button heads 2 to 3 cm across, vivid purple-magenta, well spaced, the top one largest and first to open; dark red-purple bracts. The model's leafy stem is right in kind; its heads are pale pink dots a few millimetres across. Recorded 1.4 cm and pink.

Lilium philadelphicum.note: Photographs: a single upright stem with whorls of narrow leaves and one or two large, upward-facing, red-orange cups of six spotted tepals. Model: a single stem with whorled leaves and two flat orange stars at the top; it reads as a wood lily, but the flowers lie flat and sideways like butterflies instead of upturned cups, and are orange rather than scarlet-orange.

earlier.note: One straight stem with narrow leaves scattered up it and a whorl of them just under the flower; one to three upright, open cups 6 to 8 cm across, six orange-red tepals narrowed to stalks at the base, yellow and purple-spotted inside. The model is a grass tussock with orange and brown stars floating over it. The flower's size and count are right; it is on the wrong body and too orange, with no spotted throat.

Linnaea borealis.note: Photographs: a trailing carpet of thin runners with pairs of small, round, glossy leaves, and thin forked stalks each with two nodding pale pink bells. Model: a flat dark green octagonal plate on the ground with sprigs round its edge and a few stalks of pink flecks; the carpet of paired leaves and the twin bells are not there.

earlier.note: Thin trailing stems with pairs of small, round, glossy evergreen leaves 1 to 2 cm, and thread-like stalks a finger high that fork at the top to hang two pink bells side by side. The model is a mound of large plates with four pink specks on it: no upright forked stalks, which are the plant's name.

Linum lewisii.note: Photographs: a clump of thin, wiry, arching stems with fine narrow leaves, covered in open sky-blue five-petalled flowers 2 to 3 cm. Model: a clump of thin arching stems covered in open pale blue flowers; reads as blue flax. A little denser in bloom than most of the photographs.

earlier.note: A tuft of many wiry stems, closely set with tiny narrow leaves, arching at the top with sky-blue flowers 2.5 to 3 cm: five broad petals with darker veins and a yellow eye; round seed capsules on curved stalks. One of the better models: thin leafy stems and pale blue flowers at the top. Half the flowers render near-black navy, and it has three stems where the plant has dozens.

Lonicera dioica.note: Photographs: a twining vine scrambling over shrubs, its paired leaves fused into a round disc under each cluster of orange-red to yellow tubular flowers, then red berries. Model: drawn on a red-stemmed host, the pair is one dense shrub of feathery sprays dotted with white specks; the vine, its fused leaf discs and its orange flowers are not seen.

earlier.note: A twining woody vine with opposite, oval, blue-green leaves, whitish beneath; the top pair below each flower cluster is joined into one disc round the stem, which stays on the vine all winter as a papery cup. The flowers are a bunch of yellow to orange-red tubes with long stamens in that cup; then red berries in it. The model's vine is two hanging chains of small leaves with specks in the air.

Lonicera involucrata.note: Photographs: a shrub with large opposite elliptic leaves, bright green; paired yellow tubular flowers in green then red bracts; shiny black berries set in deep red bracts. Model: a rounded shrub of small paired leaves along twigs that read as pinnate fronds, with red specks; the leaves are far too small and the flowers are drawn red (the recorded colour).

earlier.note: An upright shrub with large pointed opposite leaves; pairs of yellow tubular flowers in the leaf axils, cupped in green bracts that turn dark red around a pair of shiny black berries. The catalogue has the flower red and the fruit red: the red is the bracts, the flowers are yellow and the berries black. The model's flowers are specks floating outside the bush.

Lysimachia ciliata.note: Photographs: a leafy upright plant with paired broad ovate leaves all the way up and nodding yellow star flowers 2 cm across from the upper leaf joints. Model: thin stems with small sparse paired leaves, a few tiny yellow dots and one big dark leaf-like card at the top of each stem; far too sparse and the flowers too small to see.

earlier.note: Upright stems with opposite, broad, pointed oval leaves on fringed stalks; yellow five-petalled flowers 2 cm, each petal ending in a small point, nodding singly on long stalks from the upper leaf axils. It is recorded as a raceme. The model has thin grass-blade leaves and a column of orange and brown flecks round the stem top.

Maianthemum amplexicaule.note: Photographs: an arching, unbranched stem with two rows of large broad clasping leaves and a fluffy plume of tiny white flowers at the tip; red berries later. Model: two thin upright stems with small scattered leaves and tiny white dots at the top; the stems should arch, the leaves be larger and in two rows, and the plume fuller.

earlier.note: One arching, zigzag stem with 6 to 12 broad, pointed, pleated leaves in two flat rows, like a ladder, ending in a creamy plume 5 to 12 cm; then a bunch of red speckled berries at the stem tip. The model is a spiral pagoda of plates round a straight pole, the flowers a few specks to one side, the berries scattered in the air.

Maianthemum canadense.note: Photographs: a carpet of shoots each with one to three glossy heart-shaped leaves and a short, dense spike of tiny white star flowers, then speckled then red berries. Model: a loose colony of single stalks with a leaf or two and a few white specks, red berries in July; it reads as the plant, but the carpet is far thinner and the spike a loose scatter.

earlier.note: A carpet of separate small stems, each with one to three glossy heart-based oval leaves and, on flowering stems, one short dense spike of tiny white four-part stars standing above them; berries speckled, then red. The model is one big stack of plates with white stars scattered in its centre and red balls on top.

Maianthemum stellatum.note: Photographs: a colony of arching unbranched stems with two rows of broad, clasping, lance leaves and a short raceme of white star flowers at the tip, then green-striped then red berries. Model: a colony of thin upright stems with narrow leaves; no flowers in May, and the leaves are too narrow for its broad clasping ones; the August berries read.

earlier.note: One arching, unbranched stem with narrow lance leaves in two flat rows, folded along the midrib and clasping the stem, ending in a short raceme of 5 to 10 white six-pointed stars; berries green with dark stripes, then dark red, at the stem tip. The model is a spiral pagoda of broad plates with no flower (none is recorded) and red dots through the stack.

Matteuccia struthiopteris.note: Photographs: a vase-shaped crown of large, arching, feathery fronds up to 1.5 m, bright green, finely divided, narrowing to the base like an ostrich plume; brown fertile fronds in the centre in winter. Model: a bundle of upright stalks set with a few dark leaf-shaped blades; no fronds, no vase, nothing feathery.

earlier.note: A vase of large fronds to 1.5 m, each a broad feather widest above the middle and tapering to the base, of 20 to 60 pairs of narrow, deeply cut leaflets set close together, bright green; fiddleheads in spring; short dark-brown fertile fronds that stand all winter. The model is a few thin wands with a dozen separate dark ovals each: it reads as a willow twig, not a fern.

Mentha canadensis.note: Photographs: a leafy colony of square stems with paired, toothed lance leaves and dense round whorls of small lilac flowers in the leaf joints up the stem. Model: a colony of leafy stems with paired leaves and small purple specks clustered at the tops; the habit reads, but the flower whorls sit at the tip rather than ringing the stem at each leaf joint, and the stand is thinner.

earlier.note: Square stems with opposite, toothed, pointed oval leaves, and at each upper leaf pair a dense ball of tiny pale lilac to pink flowers hugging the stem, the stem tip ending in leaves. The model's whorls are the right idea, set only at the top and dark violet. The body is a pagoda of leaf plates.

Menyanthes trifoliata.note: Photographs: thick creeping stems in water with leaves of three broad oval leaflets on stalks, and a short raceme of fringed white flowers, pink in bud. Model: a bundle of flat ribbon stalks with small single blades and white stars scattered at random heights; the three-part leaf is not visible and the flowers are not on a raceme.

earlier.note: From a thick creeping stem in shallow water, long stalks each holding three broad, smooth, oval leaflets 4 to 8 cm above the surface, and a stout stalk with a dense club of white stars whose petals are thickly fringed with white hairs, pink in bud. The model is thick green posts with tiny leaves at the top and loose white stars beside them: the three big leaflets are the plant.

Mertensia paniculata.note: Photographs: a leafy, arching clump with broad, pointed, veined leaves and loose drooping clusters of tubular blue bells, pink in bud. Model: a branched clump with leaves and small blue flowers at the tips; the blue reads, but the flowers are upturned stars rather than hanging bells, and the leaves are too small and few.

earlier.note: A loose leafy clump of arching stems with pointed oval, strongly veined leaves 5 to 12 cm, and at each stem's end a drooping bunch of blue bells 1 to 1.5 cm, pink in bud. The model is a solid cone of leaf plates with a cloud of dark specks beside its top: nothing nods, nothing is blue from a step away.

Mitella nuda.note: Photographs: a creeping carpet of small round scalloped leaves in moss, with thread-thin stalks of tiny green fringed flowers. Model: one small rosette of round leaves with two thin white-flecked stalks; the leaves read right but the plant is a single rosette where it runs into a patch, and the leaf edges are smooth.

earlier.note: A few round, scalloped, hairy leaves on stalks, a few centimetres across, and a thread-thin bare stalk a hand high with a few green-yellow flowers whose petals are fringed like snowflakes. The model is a big mound of stacked angular plates with white specks in the middle: no round leaves, no stalk.

Monarda fistulosa.note: Photographs: a leafy, branched clump of grey-green paired leaves with ragged, shaggy, lilac-pink pompoms of tubular two-lipped flowers 4 to 5 cm, later round grey seed heads. Model: a leafy branched clump with smooth round pink rose-like cups on top; the shaggy lilac pompoms are rendered as smooth pink balls, and the leaves are a plain bright green.

earlier.note: A leafy clump of square stems with opposite, toothed, lance to oval grey-green leaves; each stem ends in one round shaggy head 4 to 6 cm of pale lilac tubes; dark round seed heads stand all winter. The best body so far: leafy, upright, opposite. The heads are small clusters of pink and maroon balls rather than one lilac mop, and the leaves are thin as grass.

Muhlenbergia cuspidata.note: Photographs: a dense, low tuft of fine, stiff leaves, grey-green and curly at the base, with very slender, spike-like heads on thin stems, the whole tuft turning tawny orange in autumn. Model: a dark green tussock of broad-looking blades with many slender pinkish spikes; it reads as a bunchgrass with narrow heads, but the blades are too broad and dark, and the heads too dense and pink for this wiry grass.

earlier.note: A dense tuft of wiry, thread-fine leaves from a knotty base, with very slender spike-like panicles a few millimetres wide; the whole clump turns orange-tan in autumn. The model's seed heads are tan blocks as wide as a hand, many times too thick, over wide dark straps. Seven photographs.

Myriophyllum sibiricum.note: Photographs: submerged stems with whorls of feathery, comb-like leaves, the tips of the stems rising above the water as small reddish flower spikes. Model: a scatter of flat, plain green leaf blades floating on the pond surface; no feathery whorls and no spikes.

earlier.note: Underwater stems with whorls of feather-like leaves cut into thread-fine segments, and thin reddish spikes standing a few centimetres out of the water with small flowers in whorls. The model is a scatter of broad oval leaves on the water, like a floating pondweed: the feathers are the plant.

Nassella viridula.note: Photographs: an upright bunchgrass with narrow leaves and tall, narrow, silky panicles that ripen pale straw, the awns giving a bristly fringe. Model: a dark green tussock with pale narrow heads standing above it; it reads as a bunchgrass in seed, but the leaves are much darker than the plant's soft green, and the heads are too few for its dense stand of seed stalks.

earlier.note: A dense bunch of fine, rolled, bright green leaves, with stems to 80 cm ending in a narrow, upright, greenish-then-straw panicle 10 to 25 cm long with fine wavy awns. No seed head is recorded, so the model draws white daisy shapes lying flat beside a column of wide straps.

Nuphar variegata.note: Photographs: large, round to heart-shaped leaves floating on the water, with single, thick, round, cupped yellow flowers 4 to 6 cm standing just above the surface. Model: floating heart-shaped leaves with a couple of tiny flat yellow stars; the leaves read, but the bright yellow cups that make the plant are pin-pricks.

earlier.note: Large oval floating leaves 10 to 25 cm with a deep narrow notch, crowded on the water, and yellow globes 4 to 5 cm across held just above it on thick stalks: five or six thick cupped sepals, red inside at the base, round a flat yellow disc. The model's notched pads on water read as a pond-lily. Its flowers are small flat yellow stars lying on the pads, where the plant's is a ball on a stalk.

Oenothera biennis.note: Photographs: a robust, leafy stem with lance leaves all the way up, topped by a leafy spike of large lemon-yellow four-petalled flowers 3 to 5 cm; second-year plants branch. Model: two thin stems with small leaves and small yellow flowers spaced up the top half; it reads as the plant but too thin, with too little leaf and flowers too small.

earlier.note: A flat rosette the first year; the second, a stout leafy stalk to 1.5 m, lance leaves all the way up, ending in a spike of four-petalled yellow flowers 3 to 5 cm that opens from the bottom; woody seed capsules stand through winter. The model is a hand-sized rosette under 1.5 m bare wires: the tall leafy stalk, which is the plant, is missing.

Oenothera suffrutescens.note: Photographs: a low, bushy clump of narrow grey-green leaves with spikes of small four-petalled flowers that open white and age to pink and scarlet, long stamens sticking out. Model: a clump of thin green stems with spikes of uniformly red flowers; the spike habit reads, but every flower is red where most open white (the recorded colour, which is the owner's), and the leaves are green, not grey.

earlier.note: A knee-high bunch of slender leafy stems, the leaves small, narrow and grey-green; a wand of flowers about 1 cm across with four white petals, turned to one side, that age pink then red, and long stamens. It is recorded with a 5 cm flower (the evening primrose's) and a 12 cm basal leaf: the model is a rosette under a club of huge red stars.

Opuntia fragilis.note: Photographs: a low, dense mat of small rounded spiny pads, grey-green to purplish, with pale yellow to apricot flowers. Model: dark green pads scattered in loose chains with yellow flowers; it reads as a prickly pear, but the pads are too dark and green and too thinly spread.

earlier.note: A low, tight, tangled mat of small plump joints, nearly as thick as wide, grey-green to purplish and hidden under long pale spines; pale yellow flowers 4 to 5 cm, often flushed orange or red, with red stamen stalks. The model's chains of spiny pads with yellow flowers read as a prickly-pear. The pads are scattered far apart, flat and bright green, where the plant is one dense spiny cushion.

Orthocarpus luteus.note: Photographs: a small, stiff, unbranched plant with reddish stems and narrow leaves, ending in a dense, leafy, yellow-green spike of small yellow flowers among bracts. Model: two thin green stems with yellow petals strung loosely up their upper halves; the dense, bracted, yellow spike is an open string, and the reddish stems are green.

earlier.note: A small stiff plant, one or a few upright stems crowded with narrow leaves, the upper half a dense leafy spike with golden-yellow club-shaped flowers poking out of green bracts. The model is close: narrow-leaved stems with yellow flowers up the spike. Some flowers render dark orange-brown and the leaves are long.

Oryzopsis asperifolia.note: Photographs: a woodland tuft of broad, flat, evergreen leaves lying out over the ground, with a few slender, nearly leafless stems carrying a few large pale green seeds strung along them. Model: a spreading rosette of broad blades lying out (right) under upright stems with pale dense plumes; the heads are fat cream plumes where the plant carries a thin string of few, large green seeds.

earlier.note: A woodland grass with long, broad, leathery, dark evergreen leaves that lie flat on the ground, and a few slender stems each with a narrow, sparse raceme of plump greenish-white grains. It is recorded as an open panicle; it is a narrow raceme. The model's stiff upright spray with large pale ladders hanging beside it is neither.

Osmorhiza longistylis.note: Photographs: a bushy plant of soft, fern-like, twice-divided toothed leaves held up the stems, with small, open umbels of tiny white flowers. Model: a few giant flat leaf cut-outs lying in rings on the ground and floating on bare stalks, with a few white specks; the leaves are huge plates and the plant has no leafy body.

earlier.note: A leafy woodland plant: large leaves divided two or three times into broad, toothed leaflets, on the stem as well as at the base, and small open umbels of white flowers just above the leaves. The model is five tall bare wires from a few small ladder leaves, the umbels grey flecks off to one side in the air.

Oxytropis campestris.note: Photographs (several look like another, purple, species): a low tuft of silky, grey-green pinnate leaves with leafless stalks of dense, spike-like heads of cream to pale yellow pea flowers. Model: tall stalks with loose spikes of purple pea flowers over a skirt of green fronds; the colour is the recorded purple (the owner's), the heads too loose, and the leaves green, not silky grey.

earlier.note: A tuft of silky grey-green leaves with many small leaflets, and several bare stalks each ending in a dense head of pale yellow to cream pea flowers. Its name says yellow and most of the photographs are cream; it is recorded purple (photographs 1, 3 and 13 are a purple locoweed, likely another species). The model is one stalk with purple specks scattered around it in the air.

Pascopyrum smithii.note: Photographs: a spreading sod of stiff, upright, strongly blue-grey leaves with narrow, flat spikes that ripen to straw. Model: a colony of blue-grey blades with slim upright spikes above them; reads as western wheatgrass. The blue could be stronger and the blades stiffer.

earlier.note: Stiff, strongly blue-grey, ribbed leaves standing out from the stem at an angle, in open spreading patches rather than a bunch, with a stiff upright spike 6 to 15 cm long of overlapping flat spikelets. The blue is its field mark; the model is dark olive, in a tight bunch, with tan blocks.

Penstemon gracilis.note: Photographs: slender upright stems with paired narrow leaves and a loose, one-sided raceme of pale lilac tubular two-lipped flowers. Model: slender stems with violet flowers in loose tiers; recognisable as a penstemon, but each flower is a flat flared star rather than a tube, the violet is deeper than the pale lilac, and the stems are nearly bare.

earlier.note: A slender plant: one to a few thin stems from a small rosette, pairs of narrow leaves, and a narrow open raceme of pale lilac tubes 1.5 to 2 cm, held level, with a white, purple-lined throat. The model has the tubes on the stems, the right idea, but dark violet and stubby, on a dense bush of broad blades.

Penstemon procerus.note: Photographs: a small clump of upright stems with paired narrow leaves and dense, separated whorls of small deep blue-violet tubular flowers. Model: a clump of upright stems with small lilac whorls at the tops; recognisable as a small penstemon, but the whorls are loose sprays and the colour is a pale lilac rather than deep blue-violet.

earlier.note: A low mat of small lance leaves and slender stems carrying one to several tight, ball-like whorls of small deep blue-purple tubes 1 cm long. Recorded with the genus's 2.5 cm flower and 8 cm leaf. The model's blue-purple tubes on stems are right in kind and colour; the body is a spiky rosette of long blades, like a yucca.

Persicaria amphibia.note: Photographs: a colony of leafy stems with long, glossy, lance leaves, often floating on water, each stem ending in a short, dense, bright pink spike like a thimble. Model: a colony of upright leafy stems with thin, pale pink spikes on top; the plan is right, but the spikes are thin and pale where they are fat and vivid pink.

earlier.note: In water, glossy oblong leaves floating flat and pink clubs standing above them; on land, a leafy stem with broad lance leaves. Either way the flower is a dense, solid, bright pink egg or cylinder 2 to 4 cm tall, one at each stem tip. The model is a star of stiff blades with thin strings of dots too small to see.

Petasites frigidus.note: Photographs: large, deeply lobed, hand-shaped leaves up to 20 cm, woolly white beneath, rising from creeping stems; in early spring, before the leaves, thick stalks with clustered white to pinkish flower heads. Model: a rosette of small, sharp maple-like leaves with two bare stalks and no flower heads; in April it should be mostly the white flower stalks, and later much larger leaves.

earlier.note: In April and May a thick, scaly stalk comes up before the leaves, topped with a bunch of white to pinkish heads. The leaves follow: large, cut into 5 to 7 toothed lobes like a hand, green above and white-woolly beneath, held up on long stalks. The model in April is a near-black lobed rosette flat on the ground with a few wires, and no flower, since none is recorded.

Physostegia ledinghamii.note: Photographs: upright stems with paired lance leaves and a dense, four-sided spike of pink-lilac snapdragon-like flowers at the top. Model: upright stems with paired leaves and violet flowers spaced up a long open spike; the spike is too loose and too long, and the colour bluer than the pink-lilac in the photographs.

earlier.note: Square stems with opposite, toothed lance leaves, ending in a spike of pink-purple tubular two-lipped flowers 1.5 to 2.5 cm in four rows. The model is a tower of long blades with dark purple specks hidden among them. Only four photographs.

Picea glauca.note: Photographs: a tall, dense, symmetrical spire of level to drooping branches, blue-green, with pale cones near the top. Model: a slim dark green spire; the outline reads, but the foliage is clumps of dark lobed cards rather than layered needled branches, and too dark and narrow for a white spruce's broad blue-green cone.

earlier.note: A dense cone, branches to the ground when grown in the open, blue-green. The model reads as a spruce; the flat stacked plates and the smooth pencil tip are the giveaway, and the lowest branches stop well above the ground.

Picea mariana.note: Photographs: a very narrow, often ragged spire with short drooping branches and a dense knot at the top, dark blue-green. Model: a slim dark spire of the right outline; the needle sprays read as clusters of lobed leaves at this distance, and the club top is missing.

earlier.note: A very narrow spire with short drooping branches and often a dense club at the top. The model is White Spruce's: flat stacked plates with a smooth solid cone for a tip. It reads as a spruce from a distance; the plates and the pencil-point tip are what give it away.

Pinus banksiana.note: Photographs: a scraggly, open, irregular pine with short yellow-green needles in pairs, crooked branches and many persistent curved cones. Model: a slim tree whose crown is clumps of broad lobed leaf cards, bright green; it reads as a poplar, not a pine; nothing needle-like at this distance and no cones.

earlier.note: Open irregular crown of long limbs carrying yellow-green needle tufts, curved cones held along the branches. The model is a pole with small dark whorls, a bottle brush: too narrow, too little foliage, and darker than the yellow-green in every photograph.

Polygala senega.note: Photographs: a small clump of leafy stems with lance leaves, each topped by a dense, tapering spike of tiny white flowers like a little candle. Model: a clump of thin bare green stems with a few small leaves and no flower spikes in its flowering month; the white candles that identify it are missing.

earlier.note: A clump of several unbranched stems with small lance leaves, each stem ending in a dense, tapering, white spike 2 to 4 cm long, like a small white cone. The model's clump of leafy stems is the right kind; no flower is recorded, so the white spikes that are the plant in June are missing, and the leaves are long blades.

Populus balsamifera.note: Photographs: a tall straight tree with deeply furrowed grey bark, an upright, fairly narrow crown of dark glossy leaves pale beneath; long red then green catkins in spring. Model: a slender trunk bare to half its height under a small rounded crown of pale yellow-green speckle; the crown is too small and light, more aspen than balsam poplar.

earlier.note: Tall straight bole, grey furrowed bark, an open irregular crown of ascending limbs. The model is a narrow tuft on a long square-sectioned post: the crown is too small for the trunk and the trunk reads as a fence post at the base.

Populus tremuloides.note: Photographs: a tall, slender tree with smooth chalky white-green bark marked with black, a narrow rounded crown high up of round trembling leaves, and grey hanging catkins in April. Model: a thin pale grey pole with a small leafy crown only at its very top, and in April bare twigs; the bark is grey rather than chalk white with black scars, the crown is tiny and lollipop-like, and no catkins hang.

earlier.note: A pale smooth trunk with black scars and a rounded crown of fine branches in the top third to half, the round leaves on flat stalks. The model is a very long pole with a dozen leaf clumps near the top and, leafless, almost no branches. Bark colour is right.

Potentilla anserina.note: Photographs: a low spreading patch of long pinnate leaves with many toothed leaflets, silvery beneath and often silver above, rooting along red runners, with single yellow flowers on stalks. Model: a few thin pinnate fronds splayed on the ground under small yellow flowers on stalks; the flowers read, but the leaves are too few, too thin and plain green, so the silvery carpet is lost.

earlier.note: Rosettes of feather-like leaves of many sharply toothed leaflets, green above and silver-white silky beneath, joined by long red runners; bright yellow flowers 2 cm across, one to a stalk, scattered among the leaves. One of the better mats: the pinnate leaves and the yellow read at once. The flowers are piled in one clump in the centre, and nothing shows the silver undersides or the runners.

Potentilla gracilis.note: Photographs: a clump of hand-shaped, deeply toothed basal leaves under branched stems with many bright yellow five-petalled flowers. Model: a clump of palmate basal leaves under branched stems with many yellow flowers; reads as a cinquefoil. The basal leaves are a little sparse.

earlier.note: A tuft of long-stalked leaves, each a hand of 5 to 7 toothed fingers, green above and white-woolly beneath; slender stems with an open cluster of bright yellow flowers 1.5 to 2 cm, petals notched. It is recorded pinnate; the leaf is palmate. The model's posture is close; its flower cloud is half near-black flecks.

Primula pauciflora.note: Photographs: a basal rosette of spoon-shaped leaves under a leafless stalk with an umbel of nodding magenta flowers, petals swept back like a dart, with a yellow and dark beak. Model: a rosette under one stalk with an umbel of flat, pale pink stars facing up; the swept-back nodding darts that make a shooting star are not there, and the colour is much paler than the magenta.

earlier.note: A small rosette of smooth, upright, light green spoon leaves and one or a few bare stalks, each with a spray of nodding magenta darts: petals swept straight back, a yellow and white ring, a dark point. The model's rosette, stalk and cluster are the right kind. The flowers are flat pale pink stars beside the stalk, and the rosette is near black.

Prosartes trachycarpa.note: Photographs: a branched, leafy stem with broad, glossy, pointed oval leaves held flat in two rows, small creamy bells hanging under the leaf tips, then orange-red berries. Model: a thin, nearly bare branched stalk with a few small leaves and no flowers; the broad, overlapping leaf layer that makes it a fairy bells is missing.

earlier.note: A forking, branching stem with broad, pointed, parallel-veined oval leaves held flat in two rows; one or two creamy bells hang from each branch tip under the leaves; then round, rough-skinned berries, orange to red. The model's broad oval leaves on upright stems read well. No flower is recorded for it, so it never flowers or fruits, and the stems do not fork.

Prunus pensylvanica.note: Photographs: a slender small tree with shiny red-brown bark banded with pale horizontal marks, a narrow open rounded crown of narrow glossy pointed leaves, white flowers in small umbels and tiny bright red cherries on long stalks. Model: a single dark trunk under a dense, tall, oval crown of fine dark green foliage; it reads as a young tree, but the crown is too dense and dark, the bark has no bands, and no cherries show in July.

earlier.note: Slender tree, shiny red-brown bark with horizontal lenticels, drooping lance leaves 8 cm, flat clusters of 5 to 7 white flowers in May, red cherries on long stalks. The model's leaf cards are long stiff blades pointing every way, so it reads as a palm or a yucca; no flower shows in May and no fruit in August.

Prunus virginiana.note: Photographs: a tall suckering shrub or small tree with an open crown of glossy oval leaves, white flower racemes in May, hanging clusters of red then black cherries in late summer. Model: a dense oval of dark green leaves on many stems; it could be any shrub, too compact and too dark for a 5 m chokecherry.

earlier.note: A tall dense shrub; oval leaves, widest above the middle, finely toothed; white bottlebrush racemes 8 to 10 cm long all over it in May; hanging racemes of dark red to black cherries. The model is a bundle of thick grey sticks with sparse leaf cards at the tips, with no flower in May and no fruit in August: none of what makes a chokecherry.

Pulsatilla nuttalliana.note: Photographs: a low, silky-hairy clump; in spring, before the leaves are up, large pale lavender cups with a yellow centre on short furry stems; later feathery pink-grey seed heads and finely cut grey-green leaves. Model: two clumps of finely cut green leaves under tall stalks with flat purple stars; recognisable by colour and leaf, but the flowers are flat open stars on tall stems instead of upright furry cups close to the ground, and the leaves are green rather than silky grey.

earlier.note: The flowers come before the leaves: a tuft of furry stalks, each with one cup of six pale lavender to white sepals round a big yellow centre, 4 to 6 cm; then long feathery seed heads; the leaves, cut into many narrow fingers, grow after. The model is a 60 cm near-black rosette of broad lobed leaves under two flat purple stars.

Pyrola asarifolia.note: Photographs: a rosette of round, glossy, dark green leathery leaves with a reddish stalk of nodding pink waxy bells hanging down it. Model: a rosette of round leaves under a stalk of pink flowers; reads as a pyrola, but the leaves are a flat light green rather than dark and glossy, and the flowers are open stars facing out, not nodding bells.

earlier.note: A small flat rosette of round, leathery, glossy dark leaves, and one bare reddish stalk a hand or two high carrying 8 to 20 nodding pink cups spaced up it, each with a long curved style. The model is a big spiky mound of long angular blades with pink stars in a flat cluster in the middle: the single upright stalk of bells is missing.

Ranunculus rhomboideus.note: Photographs: a very low, early plant, a few centimetres to 15 cm, with small round toothed basal leaves and shiny yellow five-petalled buttercups, then green bur-like seed heads. Model: two branched stems with narrow leaves and yellow buttercups; the flowers read, but the plant stands too tall and leggy and the round basal leaves are small slivers.

earlier.note: A small plant, a hand high: a few long-stalked basal leaves, oval to diamond-shaped with a scalloped edge and no lobes, and stem leaves cut into narrow fingers; pale lemon flowers 1.5 to 2 cm with five narrow petals. The model is a large near-black rosette of lobed leaves, wider than the plant is tall, with its flowers in a cloud off to one side.

Ratibida columnifera.note: Photographs: a branched clump of finely cut leaves under many long-stalked heads, each a tall brown column 2 to 4 cm over a skirt of drooping yellow rays. Model: a branched clump of cut leaves under many heads of brown domes on yellow rays; reads as prairie coneflower. The cones are low domes rather than tall columns, and the rays spread rather than droop.

earlier.note: Slender branching stems with sparse grey-green leaves cut into narrow fingers; each long bare stalk ends in a column 2 to 4 cm tall, grey-green then dark brown, with 4 to 8 yellow rays hanging down from its base. The model is a pagoda of broad leaf plates with small flat heads lying among them: no column, which is the plant's name.

Ribes americanum.note: Photographs: an upright, open shrub of leafy stems with maple-like lobed leaves, drooping strings of yellow-green bell flowers among the new leaves in May, then black currants. Model: a dense dome of lobed leaves with red berries; the April picture is bare twigs with yellow specks, though the shrub flowers with its leaves out; the fruit is drawn red (recorded) where the photographs show black, and it is the same body as the other currants.

earlier.note: A leafy mound with maple-like lobed leaves dotted with gold glands beneath; drooping racemes of creamy yellow bell flowers; black berries. The model is a believable leafy mound. Its berries are red, and the catalogue records them red: they are black. In April its flowers are specks floating above bare sticks.

Ribes glandulosum.note: Photographs: a low, sprawling shrub of trailing stems with maple-like lobed leaves, small white flowers in upright racemes, and bristly red berries. Model: a dome of lobed leaves on bare stilts with dark red berry strings at the edge; the leaf outline is right but the shrub stands as an umbrella instead of trailing on the ground, and the leaves are too dark.

earlier.note: A low sprawling currant; maple-like leaves of 5 to 7 sharp lobes; upright racemes of small white-pink flowers; red bristly berries. The model is a low spreading bush with red berry strings, some hanging in the air beside it; the leaves are plain ovals.

Ribes hudsonianum.note: Photographs: an open, upright shrub with large, maple-like, three to five-lobed leaves, erect racemes of small white flowers in spring and black currants in summer. Model: a dense rounded shrub of lobed leaves; the leaf outline is right, but it reads the same as the other currants and cranberries, and the few dark fruit are lost in the leaves.

earlier.note: An upright shrub with large maple-like leaves of 3 to 5 lobes; upright racemes of small white flowers in May; black berries. The model is a believable leafy bush, the best of the shrubs so far; its leaves are unlobed plates, no flower shows in May, and some of its black berries hang outside the plant.

Ribes lacustre.note: Photographs: a low arching shrub with bristly stems, glossy maple-like lobed leaves held low, drooping strings of small saucer flowers and black berries. Model: an umbrella of lobed leaves on tall bare stilts with red berry strings on top; the leaf outline is right, but the canopy should come to the ground and the fruit is black, not red.

earlier.note: A low sprawling shrub with bristly stems; glossy maple-like leaves cut into 3 to 5 lobes; drooping racemes of small pinkish saucer flowers; dark purple-black bristly berries. The model is bare sticks with a few small plain leaves; its berries are red and some hang in the air beside the plant; in May its flowers are a cloud above it.

Ribes oxyacanthoides.note: Photographs: a low, sprawling, prickly shrub of arching stems with small, deeply lobed leaves, pale flowers hanging under the stems in May, and round green to purple-black gooseberries. Model: an umbrella of lobed leaves on dark bare stilts with tiny red dots; it should be a low, leafy tangle to the ground, its prickly pale stems show, and the berries are drawn red where they ripen dark purple.

earlier.note: A low bristly, thorny shrub; small rounded leaves cut into 3 to 5 lobes; flowers singly or in twos and threes in the axils, greenish white; smooth berries ripening purple-black. It is recorded as a raceme of 12 and a red berry. The model's two bare elbowed canes reaching out sideways are the first thing the eye sees.

Ribes triste.note: Photographs: a low, sprawling shrub with large, three-to-five-lobed maple-like leaves, drooping racemes of small reddish-purple flowers, and hanging strings of bright red currants. Model: a low dome of lobed leaves on stilts with red berry strings at the edge; the leaves and red strings read, but the shrub should lie low and sprawl, and the May flowers do not show.

earlier.note: A low sprawling currant of the forest floor; broad leaves of 3 to 5 shallow lobes; drooping racemes of small reddish-purple saucer flowers; strings of bright red, shiny currants. The model is a low leafy bush with red berry strings, close in kind. Its leaves are plain ovals and several of its berry strings hang in the air well outside the plant.

Rosa acicularis.note: Photographs: an open shrub of densely bristly reddish stems with pinnate leaves, single pink roses 5 cm, and from August elongated, pear-shaped red hips. Model: a dense column of pinnate leaves with a handful of pink flowers; the August picture shows no hips at all, though the hips are what mark a wild rose for half the year.

earlier.note: Slender bristly stems; leaves of 5 to 7 oval toothed leaflets; pink flowers 5 to 7 cm across with a yellow centre, many open at once; red pear-shaped hips. The model's leaflets are narrow blades, so it reads as a willow; the flowers are a few specks, some dark; no hip shows in August.

Rosa arkansana.note: Photographs: a low, open, suckering shrub of thin prickly stems, pinnate leaves of several toothed leaflets, and pink five-petalled roses 4 to 6 cm with yellow centres, then red hips. Model: a low, dense, rounded mound of pinnate leaves with pink flowers round its edge; it reads as a low rose, but it is a solid mound rather than open stems, and the flowers are smaller than life.

earlier.note: A low rose, knee high at most, dying back hard; leaves of 9 to 11 leaflets; pink flowers 4 to 5 cm in clusters at the stem tips; round red hips. The model reads as a low rose in flower, the flowers at their size. The base is a thick trunk, the leaflets are narrow, and no hip shows in September.

Rosa woodsii.note: Photographs: an open thicket of slender, prickly, red-brown canes with small pinnate leaves, pink roses 4 to 5 cm, and clusters of round, glossy red hips held all autumn and into winter. Model: a dense round dome of pinnate leaves with small pink flowers; the September picture turns the whole dome orange-gold with no red hips visible; it is the same body as the prickly wild rose.

earlier.note: A thicket of red-brown prickly stems; leaves of 5 to 9 oval toothed leaflets; pink flowers 4 to 5 cm, several together; clusters of red hips. The model is thick brown sticks with narrow-bladed leaves, a few pink specks floating above it and no hips.

Rubus arcticus.note: Photographs: a low patch of three-part toothed leaves close to the ground with single magenta-pink five-petalled flowers held just above them, then red raspberry-like fruit. Model: thin single stalks standing well above a few small leaves, each with one pink flower; the colour and single flower are right, but the stalks are too tall and bare and the leaves too few and small.

earlier.note: A hand-high plant in patches: leaves of three rounded, toothed leaflets, and one deep rose-magenta flower 2 to 2.5 cm per shoot, the petals narrow at the base; a red raspberry. The model is the Dewberry's tuft under a bouquet of pale pink: too many flowers, too pale, on narrow blades.

Rubus idaeus.note: Photographs: a dense patch of arching, bristly canes, leafy throughout with three-to-five-part toothed leaves, pale beneath, white flowers and red raspberries. Model: a single narrow, upright column of leaf cards on a few stems, with a few white and red specks; it should be a broad, low patch of arching canes, not a narrow pillar.

earlier.note: Arching bristly canes forming a thicket as wide as it is tall; leaves of 3 to 5 broad toothed leaflets, pale beneath; white flowers with small narrow petals; red raspberries. The model is a narrow upright bundle of straight canes on one stem with narrow blades: the right height, none of the arching or the broad leaves.

Rubus pubescens.note: Photographs: a low trailing plant with runners, leaves of three sharply toothed leaflets close to the ground, small white flowers and red raspberry-like fruit. Model: a colony of single thin stalks with three-part leaves and white flowers; the leaves read, but the stalks stand too tall and bare, the patch is too thin, and the leaflets have no teeth.

earlier.note: Long runners trailing over the forest floor with short upright shoots, each leaf of three broad, sharply toothed, pointed leaflets; one to three small white flowers with narrow upright petals; a dark red raspberry of a few large beads. The model is a tuft of narrow blades from one point under a big bouquet of white flowers: a different, showier plant.

Sagittaria cuneata.note: Photographs: arrow-shaped leaves on long stalks rising from shallow water, whorls of white three-petalled flowers with yellow centres on a separate stalk. Model: arrowhead leaves on stalks and white flowers above, which reads as the plant; the leaves are a dark, flat green and stiff, and the flowers float as a loose cloud rather than in tiers on a stalk.

earlier.note: A tuft of long-stalked arrowhead leaves, the two back lobes long and pointed, and a stalk with whorls of three white flowers 2 to 2.5 cm, three round petals round a yellow centre. One of the best models: arrowhead leaves on stalks and flowers in whorls. Half the flowers render grey-black and the leaves are a dark teal where the plant is a light yellow-green.

Salix bebbiana.note: Photographs: a large shrub to small tree of several stems with dull grey-green elliptic leaves, an irregular spreading crown, woolly seed catkins in June. Model: a narrow column of several trunks with a blotchy crown in clumps of dark green and yellow-green speckle; the crown is too narrow and its colour patchy and too yellow.

earlier.note: A big shrub or small tree of many crooked stems, bushy from low down; dull green elliptic leaves, pale beneath; yellow catkins on bare twigs in April. The model is three or four thick straight trunks with leaves only at the top, and in April it is bare sticks with no catkins.

Salix discolor.note: Photographs: a large shrub of many upright grey-brown stems with broad elliptic leaves, bluish-white beneath; in March fat silky grey catkins on bare twigs. Model: an upright many-stemmed shrub with a light green crown of oval leaves, and in March bare twigs; the July shrub reads as a willow, but the March picture shows no silver catkins, which are the plant's whole point at that season.

earlier.note: A tall many-stemmed willow, leafy to the ground; elliptic leaves, blue-white beneath; silvery furry catkins along bare twigs in March and April, which is the whole of what it is known for. The model is a narrow bundle of thick straight poles with leaves at the top, and in March it is bare sticks with no catkins.

Salix exigua.note: Photographs: a thicket of slender, upright, sparsely branched stems with long very narrow grey-green leaves, giving a fine, airy, grey look. Model: a colony of thin upright stems with fine narrow leaves, airy and pale; reads as sandbar willow. The leaves are a yellower green than the photographs' silvery grey.

earlier.note: A thicket of slender wands thick with long, very narrow silvery grey-green leaves: a soft feathery grey mass. The model is a grey skeleton with slivers, which reads as dead or thorny. Many of the photographs are from the American south-west; the form is the same.

Salix interior.note: Photographs: a dense thicket of slender upright stems with long, very narrow, grey-green leaves; yellow catkins with the new leaves in spring. Model: a thicket of thin upright stems with fine narrow pale leaves; reads as sandbar willow. In April the stems are bare with a faint yellow haze where the catkins should show clearly, and the leaves are yellower than the grey-green in the photographs.

earlier.note: Thickets of slender upright wands on sandbars, each closely set with long narrow leaves, green to silvery; slim yellow catkins on leafy shoots. The model is three thick trunks with tufts of slivers: nothing of the dense leafy wand.

Salix petiolaris.note: Photographs: a shrub of many slender upright reddish-brown stems with narrow lance leaves, grey-white beneath, catkins before the leaves. Model: a dense conical mass of narrow leaves in two greens on many thin dark stems; the leaves read as willow, but it is a solid cone where the plant is open and upright, and the red-brown stems do not show.

earlier.note: A dense clump of slender stems thick with narrow lance leaves 5 to 10 cm long, green above and silvery beneath; catkins in April and May. The model is a grey skeleton with slivers for leaves: it reads as a dead bush. In April it has no catkins.

Schizachne purpurascens.note: Photographs: a loose woodland tuft of narrow leaves with slender, few-flowered, nodding heads of purplish spikelets with long awns. Model: a tussock with arching stems of pinkish-purple spikelets; it reads as a soft purple-headed grass, but the heads are too many and too full for a few-flowered one, and the awns do not show.

earlier.note: A loose tuft of narrow leaves with slender stems ending in a sparse, drooping panicle of a few large purplish spikelets 2 cm long with spreading awns, hanging from hair-fine branches. The seed head is recorded nodding; the model shows faint pale flecks standing upright in a column of wide straps.

Schoenoplectus acutus.note: Photographs: a dense stand of tall, round, leafless grey-green stems with a small cluster of brown spikelets drooping from just below the tip of each. Model: a stand of tall grey-green stems with small brown tufts; reads as a bulrush, but the tufts sit at many heights partway down the stems rather than just under the tips.

earlier.note: Round, smooth, leafless, grey-green stems to 2.5 m, as thick as a finger at the base and tapering to a point, in open stands; a drooping bunch of red-brown spikelets hangs from one side just below the stem's tip. The model is the cattail's column of flat blades with small orange plates floating beside it: it has no flat blades at all.

Schoenoplectus pungens.note: Photographs: a stand of stiff, triangular, leafless green stems with a small cluster of brown spikelets stuck to one side a little below the tip. Model: a stand of tall thin stems with small brown clusters on the side partway up; reads as three-square. The stand is thinner than the dense colony in the photographs.

earlier.note: Stands of stiff, sharply three-sided, leafless stems, each with a tight knot of one to five red-brown spikelets that sits on the side of the stem a few centimetres below its sharp tip. The model is a tussock of wide flat straps with cream ovals on sticks: the plant has no flat leaves, and its head is on the stem, not on a stalk.

Scirpus microcarpus.note: Photographs: a leafy clump of broad, flat, bright green leaves with a large, open, spreading umbel of small brown-green spikelet clusters at the top, the leafy bracts below it. Model: a broad leafy tussock under a spray of stalks carrying dark clustered heads; reads as a bulrush. The umbel stands well above the leaves on bare stalks, where it should sit just over them among leafy bracts.

earlier.note: A stout, leafy stem with broad, bright yellow-green leaves up it, topped by a wide, flat, much-branched spray 10 to 20 cm across of many small dark green-brown clusters, with long leafy bracts beneath like the ribs of an umbrella. The model is a dark narrow column with a few pale flecks: the broad starburst head is missing.

Scutellaria galericulata.note: Photographs: a low, leafy, branching plant with paired lance leaves and blue-violet hooded flowers in pairs at the leaf joints, each facing one way. Model: an open spray of thin stems with violet flowers scattered all over; the colour is right, but the plant is too airy and bare and the flowers float free of the leaf joints.

earlier.note: A slender plant with opposite, short, scallop-edged lance leaves 2 to 5 cm, and blue-violet hooded flowers 1.5 to 2 cm in pairs in the leaf axils, both turned to one side. The model scatters its flowers through the plant, which is close to right. They are near-black violet, and the body is a dense bush of long stiff blades.

Shepherdia argentea.note: Photographs: a thorny, much-branched shrub of silvery grey twigs and narrow, silvery, oblong leaves in pairs; tiny yellow flowers on bare twigs in April-May, then masses of bright red berries. Model: a tall narrow crown of silver frond-like sprays on a few stems; the silver reads, but in May it is in full leaf with no flowers, in August there are no red berries visible, and the paired leaves read as feathers.

earlier.note: A thorny shrub, silvery on both sides of its narrow oblong leaves, pale grey twigs; tiny yellow flowers on bare twigs in May; masses of bright red berries along the branches. The model has the silver, which is most of the plant; the trunks are too thick and the berries do not show.

Shepherdia canadensis.note: Photographs: an open shrub with brown scurfy twigs and opposite oval leaves, dull green above and silvery with rusty dots beneath; translucent red berries in July. Model: a dense shrub of silvery white sprays of paired leaves that read as pinnate fronds; far too silver (only the undersides are), and no berries.

earlier.note: A rounded leafy shrub; opposite oval leaves, dark green above, silvery with rust-brown dots beneath; brown scurfy twigs; red berries clustered tight at the nodes along the stems. The model is bare forked sticks with a few grey leaves, and its berries are red specks scattered through the air around it.

Sisyrinchium montanum.note: Photographs: a small fan of flat grass-like leaves and flattened stems with one to three blue-violet six-pointed stars with a yellow eye. Model: a grassy fan with a cluster of blue stars at the top of the stems; recognisable. The blue is paler and skier than the violet-blue in the photographs and there are too many flowers at once.

earlier.note: A small stiff tuft of flat, narrow, pale green iris-like blades, each flat stem carrying one or two blue-violet stars 1.5 to 2 cm with six pointed tepals and a yellow eye, held at the top beside a pointed bract; round seed capsules. The model reads as the plant: a tuft of blades with blue flowers at the top. It is too dense and dark, and half the flowers render navy.

Sium suave.note: Photographs: a tall, upright, branched stem in wet ground with pinnate leaves of long, narrow, toothed leaflets, topped by flat white umbels in July. Model: one stem with tiers of pinnate leaves of short oval leaflets and no visible umbels in its July picture; the leaflets are too short and broad and the white umbels are missing.

earlier.note: A tall, hollow, ridged stem with leaves of 7 to 17 narrow, saw-toothed lance leaflets, topped by several domed white umbels 5 to 12 cm across. The model's ladder leaves up a tall stem are the right kind. Its umbels are small grey smudges where the plant's are broad white domes, and the leaves are dark teal.

Solidago altissima.note: Photographs: a dense stand of tall, leafy stems crowded with lance leaves, each topped by a large, arching, branched plume of golden yellow. Model: a few thin stems with sparse leaves and a faint haze of yellow specks around their tops; the golden plumes that make a goldenrod stand are missing.

earlier.note: A tall leafy stem, rough and grey-downy, under a broad pyramid of arching, one-sided branches solid with small yellow heads; grey-tan fluff after. The model is a few thin stems and a faint dust of dots, nothing yellow from two steps away.

Solidago gigantea.note: Photographs: tall leafy stems crowded with lance leaves, ending in a large branched plume of arching yellow sprays. Model: tall leafy stems with a few yellow specks drifting loosely round their upper halves; the stems read, but the dense golden plume at the top is missing.

earlier.note: A tall, smooth, leafy stem topped by a large pyramid of bright yellow on arching, one-sided branches; the fluffy tan seed plumes stand into winter. The model is a few thin stems with small leaves and a faint dust of dots: nothing yellow from two steps away.

Solidago glutinosa.note: Photographs: a short plant with a basal rosette of spoon leaves under a stiff stem ending in a dense, narrow wand of yellow heads. Model: a basal rosette and thin stems with yellow stars scattered loosely round their upper half; the rosette is right, but the dense yellow wand is an open scatter.

earlier.note: A small goldenrod: a tuft of spoon-shaped basal leaves and one unbranched stem ending in a narrow, dense, upright wand of yellow heads about 1 cm across. The model's yellow stars are visible, more than on the tall goldenrods; they are scattered round a star-shaped tower of long blades, not gathered in a wand.

Solidago lepida.note: Photographs: leafy stems crowded with lance leaves to the top, ending in a dense club or plume of tiny bright yellow heads. Model: leafy stems with yellow specks floating loosely around and above them; no dense plume at the stem tips, so it reads as stems in a yellow haze.

earlier.note: A leafy stem with many toothed lance leaves, topped by a dense pyramid or plume of bright yellow, 10 to 20 cm tall, the branches often arching to one side. The model in August, its flowering, shows a dozen yellow specks among stiff blades: a goldenrod with no gold.

Solidago missouriensis.note: Photographs: upright leafy stems ending in a dense, arching, one-sided plume of tiny golden heads. Model: a bundle of stems with a loose cloud of yellow specks scattered round them from top to bottom; no plume at the tip, so it reads as a plant in a yellow haze.

earlier.note: A low, smooth goldenrod: narrow three-veined lance leaves, larger at the base, and one compact bright yellow plume 5 to 15 cm, often nodding to one side. The model is a dense tuft of long stiff blades with a dozen small yellow stars lost among them.

Solidago rigida.note: Photographs: stiff, leafy, grey-green stems with broad oval leaves topped by a dense, flat-topped cluster of golden-yellow heads. Model: a bundle of thin bare stems with faint pale flat sprays at the top; the golden dome that is the plant's mark is a pale haze, and the leafy stems are bare.

earlier.note: A stout, hairy, grey-green plant with broad, stiff, oval leaves, large and long-stalked at the base and clasping up the stem, under a dense flat-topped head of large deep yellow flowers. It is recorded as a plume with lance leaves; it is the one goldenrod here with a flat top and oval leaves. The model is a thin stem with small leaves and a sparse spray of dots.

Sparganium eurycarpum.note: Photographs: a stand of long, keeled, strap-like leaves with zigzag flowering stems carrying round spiky burs, the female heads large and green, the male heads small and pale. Model: a grassy clump with stems of small green balls above it; it reads as a bur-reed, but the burs are too small and too even, and the stems too far above the leaves.

earlier.note: A clump of long, stiff, keeled, bright yellow-green leaves, with a zigzag branching stalk carrying round white pompoms of flowers that become green spiky burs 2 to 3 cm across, like small maces. The model is a dark tight column of blades with no flower in June and no burs: the round burs are how the plant is known.

Spiraea alba.note: Photographs: an upright shrub of many unbranched wand-like stems with narrow toothed leaves, each stem tipped with a narrow, pyramid-shaped white flower spike; brown seed spikes held through winter. Model: a dense, rounded bush of narrow leaves with white flower sprays all over its outside; it reads as a white-flowering shrub, but the upright wands, each ending in one spike, are lost in a rounded mass.

earlier.note: Slender upright wands, closely set with small toothed lance leaves, each ending in a dense white steeple of tiny flowers 5 to 15 cm tall; the brown seed heads stand through winter. It is recorded as a flat-topped cluster; it is a cone (a panicle). The model is thick canes with long stiff blades and specks floating above.

Spiranthes romanzoffiana.note: Photographs: a short plant with a few narrow leaves at the base and a stout, dense spiral spike of creamy hooded flowers. Model: a tall bare stem with a thin dotted line of white specks, and a separate tall green blade beside it; the spike should be a fat cream column, and the plant is too tall and thin.

earlier.note: A few narrow leaves at the base and one stem ending in a dense, thick, cream-white spike 5 to 10 cm tall, the hooded flowers packed in three spiralling rows. The model is a tall dense tuft of grass blades with small grey dots scattered loosely in the air above it.

Stachys pilosa.note: Photographs: hairy upright stems with paired toothed leaves and a spike of tiered whorls of pale pink-lilac two-lipped flowers. Model: upright leafy stems with paired leaves and small violet whorls at the tops; it reads as a mint relative, but the whorls are bunched at the top instead of tiered down a spike, and the colour is a deeper violet than the pale pink.

earlier.note: A hairy square stem with opposite, toothed, lance to oblong leaves, ending in a spike of separate whorls of pale pink-lilac two-lipped flowers, the lower lip spotted purple. The model's whorls spaced up the stem are the right idea. They are dark violet dots, where the plant is pale pink, and the leaves are thin grass blades.

Stuckenia pectinata.note: Photographs: dense, bushy masses of thread-fine branching leaves under the water, often lying on the surface in streaming mats, with small spikes of brownish fruit. Model: a dozen tiny slivers scattered on the pond surface; it shows something in the water, but not the thick waving mass of threads.

earlier.note: Dense underwater beds of thread-fine leaves on much-branched stems, all combed one way by the current, bright green to olive; small beaded spikes that barely reach the surface. The model shows a dozen short blades on the water, which is fair for a submerged plant seen from the bank; the plant is far denser and its leaves are threads.

Symphoricarpos albus.note: Photographs: an open shrub of thin arching twigs with small round to oval paired leaves, blue-green, small pink bells and, from late summer, clusters of round white berries that last into winter. Model: a dense upright mass of paired leaves in sprays that read as pinnate fronds, in a plain mid-green; the white berries that make the plant are not on the July picture.

earlier.note: A fine twiggy shrub of slender arching stems; small roundish opposite leaves, dull blue-green; tiny pink bells; clusters of white berries that stay into winter and are how most people know it. The model's canes are thick, its flowers hover above it in the air, and the white berries do not show.

Symphoricarpos occidentalis.note: Photographs: a low thicket of upright twigs with paired, thick, oval, grey-green leaves, small pink bells in clusters at the tips, and clusters of greenish-white berries that blacken over winter. Model: a dense dome of paired leaves arranged into feather-like fronds, plain green; in September it turns yellow with no white berries showing. It reads as a fern-leaved bush, not a snowberry, and it is the same body as common snowberry.

earlier.note: A dense colony of upright stems to a metre, oval grey-green leaves 3 to 6 cm, clusters of small pink-white flowers at the tips and in the axils, greenish-white berries that blacken over winter. The model is a pile of large bright plates, like a cabbage; no flower shows in July and no berry in September.

Symphyotrichum boreale.note: Photographs: slender stems in wet ground with narrow leaves and a few white daisies 2 to 3 cm with yellow centres. Model: very thin, nearly bare stems with tiny yellow specks at the tips; the white rays do not show, so no daisy reads.

earlier.note: A very slender plant: one thin reddish stem with a few narrow, grass-like leaves, and a few white to pale lilac daisies 1.5 to 2 cm at the top. The model is a dense column of broad stiff blades, like a yucca, with tan specks above it.

Symphyotrichum ciliolatum.note: Photographs: a leafy clump with heart-shaped lower leaves and branched tops crowded with lilac-blue daisies about 2.5 cm. Model: a few big heart leaves at the base under thin, nearly bare stems with a few tiny pink and yellow specks; the lilac daisies are lost, so it reads as stems gone to seed.

earlier.note: Heart-shaped lower leaves on winged stalks, smaller lance leaves up the stem, and an open cluster of pale blue-violet daisies 2 to 3 cm with 12 to 25 rays. The model is the same thin stem and grass blades as Smooth Aster under a column of pink-tan specks.

Symphyotrichum ericoides.note: Photographs: a bushy, much-branched plant with tiny narrow leaves, its arching branches crowded with small white daisies like a white haze in late summer. Model: an upright broom of bare green stems with barely visible white specks; neither the bushiness nor the white haze reads.

earlier.note: A bushy, much-branched plant with tiny needle-like leaves 1 to 2 cm, the branches lined on one side with crowds of small white daisies 1 cm across. Recorded with 8 cm leaves and 2.5 cm heads (the genus default). The model is thin stems with long grass blades and a haze of tan specks.

Symphyotrichum falcatum.note: Photographs: a bushy, much-branched plant of small, narrow, grey-green leaves covered with white daisies with yellow centres along its upper branches. Model: three thin, nearly bare stems with a few white heads at the tips; the right flower, but too few and on bare wires where the plant is bushy and crowded with them.

earlier.note: A slender, grey-hairy, branching stem with small narrow leaves 2 to 4 cm, the branches lined with white daisies 2 cm across. Recorded with 8 cm leaves on a 35 cm plant, so the model is a rosette of sword blades like a yucca, with the flowers in a flat cap. The flower heads themselves read as white daisies, the best of the asters.

Symphyotrichum hesperium.note: Photographs: a colony of leafy stems with long narrow leaves, the tops branched with many white to pale lilac daisies 2 to 3 cm. Model: a colony of thin, sparsely leaved stems with tiny pale dots at the tips; the daisies do not read.

earlier.note: A leafy stem with narrow lance leaves and pale lilac to white daisies 2 to 2.5 cm. The model is the same thin stem and tan specks as the other asters. Only six photographs, none of the whole plant, and two from Texas.

Symphyotrichum laeve.note: Photographs: a clump of smooth, blue-green clasping leaves and branched tops crowded with lilac-blue daisies 2 to 3 cm with yellow centres. Model: a clump of thin stems with sparse leaves and only tiny pinkish specks at the tips; the lilac daisies, the whole look of the plant in September, are lost.

earlier.note: A bushy plant of smooth blue-green stems and clasping lance leaves, covered in late summer with dozens of violet-blue daisies 2 to 3 cm with yellow centres. The model's single leafy stem is right in kind. Its flowers are a thin haze of tiny tan and orange specks, not violet daisies; the plant does not read as in flower at all.

Symphyotrichum lanceolatum.note: Photographs: a leafy, branched colony crowded in autumn with white (sometimes pale lilac) daisies 1.5 to 2.5 cm with yellow centres. Model: a colony of thin, sparsely leaved stems with tiny pale specks; the white daisies do not read.

earlier.note: Tall leafy stems in colonies with narrow lance leaves, the top a leafy pyramid of many white daisies 1.5 to 2 cm with yellow centres that redden. The model's stem and leaves are right in kind; in September the body is olive-brown, and the flowers are a few tan specks.

Symphyotrichum puniceum.note: Photographs: a tall, leafy, branched plant with reddish hairy stems, clasping lance leaves and many pale blue-violet daisies about 3 cm. Model: a tall bundle of thin green stems with sparse narrow leaves and no visible flowers in its August picture; it reads as a stand of bare stems.
