earlier.note: A stout, bristly, purple-red stem to 1.8 m with clasping lance leaves, branching above into many blue-violet daisies 2.5 to 4 cm with 30 to 60 rays. The model is one thin green stem with a scatter of pale specks: no purple stem, no blue flowers.

Thalictrum dasycarpum.note: Photographs: a tall, leafy plant with large, many-times-divided leaves of small three-lobed leaflets all up the stems, topped by a big, fluffy, branched panicle of white tassels. Model: a few tall, thin bare stalks with small ragged leaf cards and no flowers drawn; neither the lacy leaves nor the white plume read.

earlier.note: A big bushy plant to 1.8 m with purplish stems, leafy from bottom to top with blue-green leaves divided three or four times into small three-lobed leaflets, under large airy plumes of cream-white tassels. The model is a bundle of bare wires 1.8 m tall with a few tiny ladder leaves on the ground and dust at the top.

Thalictrum occidentale.note: Photographs: a lush clump of lacy blue-green leaves of many rounded, lobed leaflets, under airy panicles of drooping tassels, green-yellow or purple. Model: a few thin bare stalks over ragged leaf cards lying in rings on the ground, and no flowers; neither the lacy clump nor the tassels read.

earlier.note: A leafy woodland plant with thin, delicate leaves divided into many round three-lobed leaflets, and open panicles of nodding flowers: tassels of purple-brown stamens or small star-shaped seed clusters. The model is the same bundle of bare wires as the other meadow-rues.

Thalictrum venulosum.note: Photographs: a leafy clump of rounded, three-lobed, blue-green leaflets in loose sprays, under a narrow panicle of drooping greenish flowers with tassels of stamens. Model: a few bare thin stalks standing over ragged leaf cards lying flat on the ground; no leafy clump and no flowers to see.

earlier.note: A knee-high leafy plant: blue-green leaves divided into many rounded, three-lobed leaflets with raised veins beneath, and loose panicles of small drooping tassels, greenish to purplish. The model is six bare wires from a few tiny ladders on the ground, with dust in the air.

Thermopsis rhombifolia.note: Photographs: a spreading colony of leafy grey-green stems with three-part leaves, topped by short dense racemes of large bright yellow pea flowers; curled pods later. Model: thin bare stalks with a few leaves at the base and large yellow pea flowers spaced up them; the flowers and colour are right, but the stems are bare where they are leafy, and the green too bright.

earlier.note: Low patches, a hand or two high: three-part leaves of broad grey-green leaflets with big leafy stipules; a short dense raceme of bright yellow pea flowers 2 cm at the top of each stem; curled, sickle-shaped pods. The model draws long ladder leaves of a dozen leaflets where the plant has three, and its flowers are loose yellow and orange chips.

Typha latifolia.note: Photographs: a dense stand of broad, flat, upright leaves with thick brown cylindrical spikes at about the leaves' height. Model: a clump of narrow blades with slim brown spikes on bare stalks well above the leaves; it reads as a cattail, but the leaves are too narrow and the spikes too thin and too high.

earlier.note: A fan of long, flat, blue-green strap leaves to 2.5 m, twisting slightly, and a stiff round stalk with a dark brown sausage 10 to 18 cm long and 2 to 3 cm thick, a thinner spike above it that withers. The model reads as a cattail at once. It is one very narrow column where a clump spreads, and the spike is orange and outsized where it should be dark chocolate brown.

Urtica gracilis.note: Photographs: a dense patch of tall upright stems with paired, coarsely toothed, pointed leaves and hanging, stringy green-tan flower clusters in the leaf joints. Model: a stand of separate stems with paired leaves up their length; the habit reads, but there are no flower strings, the leaves are untoothed, and the stand too sparse for a nettle patch.

earlier.note: Tall, unbranched, square stems in dense patches, with opposite, coarsely toothed, pointed leaves 7 to 15 cm, deeply veined, and drooping green-yellow strings of tiny flowers from the upper leaf joints. The model's tall stems with opposite leaves are right in kind; the leaves are small smooth ovals a third the size, and the hanging strings are missing.

Utricularia vulgaris.note: Photographs: a free-floating feathery mass under the water with tiny bladders, and stout stalks holding yellow snapdragon-like flowers well above the surface. Model: a few green slivers on the pond surface with yellow specks among them; the flowers are not lifted on stalks and are far too small to read.

earlier.note: Free-floating feathery stems under the surface, finely branched and dotted with small dark bladders, and stout reddish stalks standing 10 to 20 cm out of the water, each with several bright yellow snapdragon-like flowers 1.5 to 2 cm with a rounded pouch. The model has a few blades on the water and yellow pinpoints: the flowers stand clear of the water and are the only part most people see.

Vaccinium myrtilloides.note: Photographs: a low, dense, twiggy shrub with small, soft, pale green leaves, clusters of small white to pink bells in May, then dusty blue berries, and bright red leaves in autumn. Model: a low dense mound of small leaves with blue berries round it; reads as a low blueberry. The leaves are darker than the soft pale green, and the May bells are too small to see.

earlier.note: A low twiggy bush, knee high; small soft elliptic leaves 2 to 4 cm, velvety, red in autumn; clusters of small pink-white bells in May; blue berries with a pale bloom in clusters. The model has the height and blue berries, some floating outside it. The leaves are large flat plates (the same body as Western Snowberry); no flower shows in May.

Vaccinium oxycoccos.note: Photographs: thread-thin trailing stems over moss with tiny pointed leaves, nodding pink shooting-star flowers on long stalks, and large dark red berries lying on the moss. Model: a flat green octagonal plate with sprigs around it and a few bare vertical stalks; nothing reads as the plant.

earlier.note: Thread-thin stems trailing over moss with tiny pointed leaves 0.5 to 1 cm, dark above and white beneath; nodding pink flowers on long red stalks, four petals swept straight back from a beak, like a shooting star; a red cranberry far larger than the leaves. The model is a mound of broad angular plates with a few specks: nothing thread-like, nothing tiny.

Veronica americana.note: Photographs: a sprawling, rooting herb of wet ground, glossy paired lance-ovate leaves on soft stems, loose sprays of small pale blue four-petalled flowers with dark lines. Model: a flat green octagonal plate on the ground ringed with sprigs and a few bare vertical stalks; no flowers in July, when it is in bloom.

earlier.note: Fleshy stems sprawling through shallow water and rooting as they go, with pairs of glossy, toothed, lance-oval leaves 2 to 5 cm, and loose racemes from the leaf joints of small violet-blue flowers with four lobes and a white eye. The model is a ring of specks on the ground and three bare wires half a metre tall, the same body as Northern Bedstraw; no flower shape is recorded.

Viburnum edule.note: Photographs: a low, open, straggly shrub of a few stems with broad three-lobed toothed leaves, small white flower clusters in June, and a few glossy red berries from August. Model: a dense, rounded mass of three-lobed leaves on a column of stems; the leaf outline is right but the shrub is far too dense and full for this open plant, and from the side it is the same body as highbush cranberry.

earlier.note: A straggling slender shrub; opposite leaves with three shallow lobes, like a small maple leaf, red in autumn; small flat white clusters; red berries in small bunches. The model's leaves are plain plates in tiers on thick canes, the flowers float above it, and the berries it draws in August sit outside the plant.

Viburnum opulus.note: Photographs: a broad, arching, many-stemmed shrub with three-lobed maple-like leaves, flat white lacecap flowers in June and hanging bunches of glossy red berries from August into winter. Model: a tall, narrow, upright column of small three-lobed leaves on a few thin stems; the leaf outline is right, but it is too narrow and upright, the leaves too small, and in July there are no green or red berries.

earlier.note: A tall shrub; opposite three-lobed maple-like leaves, red to purple in autumn; flat white lace-caps 8 to 10 cm across ringed with large sterile flowers; drooping bunches of bright red berries into winter. The model has plain dark plates on thick trunks, no flower in May, rust-brown rather than red leaves in September and no berries.

Vicia americana.note: Photographs: a slender, scrambling vine with pinnate leaves of small paired oval leaflets ending in tendrils, and loose racemes of a few purple-blue pea flowers, tangling through grass and shrubs. Model: drawn over a red-stemmed host, the pair is a tall dense shrub of fronds with white specks; the vetch is lost in it, and its purple flowers show white.

earlier.note: A slender scrambling vetch with leaves of 4 to 8 pairs of narrow oval leaflets ending in a branched tendril, and loose one-sided racemes of 3 to 9 blue-purple to red-purple pea flowers 1.5 to 2 cm. It is recorded pale pink; the photographs are purple. The model's vine is a wisp at the host's foot.

Viola adunca.note: Photographs: a small tuft of heart-shaped leaves with blue-violet spurred flowers on short stalks among and just above the leaves. Model: a small rosette of heart-shaped leaves with a few long stalks carrying small violet flowers well above it; it reads as a violet, but the flowers are too small and too high.

earlier.note: A small leafy tuft of oval to heart-shaped, round-toothed leaves on short stems, with blue-violet flowers 1 to 1.5 cm on stalks above them, the lower petal white at the base with dark lines and a hooked spur behind. The model is a mound of stacked plates with two flowers, half dark, on top; a plant in flower carries a dozen.

Viola palustris.note: Photographs: low, round to kidney leaves on stalks rising from wet moss, with pale lilac violets on short stalks just above them. Model: two rosettes of flat round leaves with long thin stalks carrying tiny lilac flowers far above; the leaves are right, but the flowers are too small and too high.

earlier.note: A few round to kidney-shaped, scalloped leaves on separate stalks from a creeping stem in wet moss, and pale lilac to nearly white flowers 1 to 1.5 cm with dark purple veins on the lower petal. It is recorded the Early Blue Violet's blue. The model is the same stack of angular plates with three small dark flowers.

Viola rugulosa.note: Photographs: a leafy colony of broad, heart-shaped, toothed leaves on stems, with white violets with a yellow throat and purple lines held among the leaves. Model: broad heart leaves lying low, with long bare stalks carrying small pink flowers high above them; the flowers are drawn pink (the recorded colour, which is the owner's) where the photographs are white, and the stalks are too tall and bare.

earlier.note: A leafy plant a hand or two high: broad heart-shaped leaves on the stems as well as at the base, and white violets 2 cm across with a yellow throat and purple lines, held just above the leaves. It is recorded pink; every photograph is white. The model is a flat near-black rosette under 30 cm bare wires with small dark blobs at the tips.

Zizia aptera.note: Photographs: a clump of heart-shaped basal leaves under leafy stems with flat-topped, compound umbels of tiny bright yellow flowers. Model: a few heart-shaped leaves at the base and tall thin stems with loose yellow sprays; the leaves are right, but the umbels are loose sprays and the plant is too sparse.

earlier.note: A rosette of long-stalked, undivided heart-shaped leaves with scalloped edges, and stems with a few three-part leaves, each ending in a flat umbel 4 to 6 cm across of tiny bright yellow flowers. It is recorded pinnate; the basal leaf is a simple heart. The model is a tall ladder-leaf plant with umbels that read as dark flecks.
